articles.title: UAE rescues 22 crew after ship catches fire
articles.summary: Abu Dhabi: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) Coast Guard rescued 22 crew members of Arab nationality after a fire broke out aboard a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman, with all those rescued reported to be in stable condition.According to the UAE National Guard, the rescue operation was launched after the ship's crew alerted a Coast Guard unit about the fire onboard.In a post on X, the UAE National Guard said, "A National Guard Coast Guard unit rescued 22 people of Arab nationalities after a fire broke out aboard a cargo ship they were on in the Gulf of Oman."Following the distress report, specialised teams immediately initiated response procedures, located the vessel and reached the ship to evacuate all 22 crew members.The rescued individuals were provided with necessary first aid before being handed over to the relevant authorities. All 22 crew members were reported to be in stable condition.The National Guard said the operation demonstrated the preparedness and operational capabilities of its personnel, highlighting their continued commitment to responding swiftly to maritime emergencies.It further emphasised that the Coast Guard's efforts were aimed at protecting lives and strengthening maritime security and safety in the region."The operation underscores the high level of readiness and field competence of National Guard personnel, as well as their constant commitment to responding swiftly to maritime incidents and emergencies," the statement added.The latest rescue operation comes amid continued maritime security efforts by the UAE authorities to respond to emergencies involving commercial vessels operating in the region.Earlier, on October 10, the UAE National Guard's Coast Guard Division had rescued 22 Asian nationals after a fire broke out aboard an oil tanker in the Arabian Gulf.In that incident, the Coast Guard activated its emergency response procedures following a distress call from the vessel, located the tanker and rescued all 22 crew members.The rescued individuals were subsequently provided first aid and handed over to the relevant authorities, with all reported to be in stable health.

articles.title: India, China stocks catch a second wind
articles.summary: The unraveling of the AI trade after the US midterm elections is forcing investors to rethink their Asia playbook, reviving demand for out-of-favor Chinese and Indian stocks as well as companies poised to benefit from easing inflation and trade tensions.Aberdeen Investments favors markets powered by stronger domestic growth, including India and Vietnam, and sees upside in Chinese technology firms. Hedge fund Lotus Asset Management is long Hong Kong equity futures, while Allianz Global Investors is looking at healthcare and consumer companies.Also Read: Bloodbath in Nasdaq, Kospi and Nikkei but why Nifty is an oasis of peace amid global rout135649455“I expect investors to diversify more broadly and reduce their concentration in the AI trade,” said Rajeev De Mello, global macro portfolio manager at Gama Asset Management SA. “This should be supportive of China and other markets where valuations are less demanding.”India could also benefit, although its dependence on imported energy remains a headwind, he added.China and India as HedgesHao Hong, chief investment officer at Lotus, said he is betting against oil and petrochemical firms and going long precious metals and Hong Kong equity futures.A Hong Kong gauge tracking mainland companies gained 5.2% last week, its best performance since March 2025.Meanwhile, some global investors are interested in using China’s onshore market exposure as a diversifier to their AI-heavy portfolio, according to Jason Lui, head of Asia-Pacific equity and derivatives strategy at BNP Paribas SA.Also Read: $5 billion in 5 days! Why FIIs are suddenly shopping Indian stocks non-stop this DiwaliIndia’s appeal, meanwhile, has grown as oil prices declined on expectations of an earlier end to the Iran war, easing a key pressure point for the energy-importing economy. The market’s lack of AI exposure is also now seen as an advantage.135649462LOGOS Asset Management’s chief investment officer Charlie Hong said he sold his shares in SK Hynix Inc., Samsung Electronics Co., Intel Corp. and Lumentum Holdings Inc. last month and has since boosted his Indian holdings with shares of new-age tech companies, financial firms and contract drug manufacturers.India’s benchmark Nifty 50 gained 8.6% last week. registering its best week since 2021, as overseas investors returned in force. Foreign funds poured a net $1.9 billion into local shares last week through Wednesday.The sudden shift has kept market participants busy. Utkarsh Singh, a Mumbai-based senior manager at SBI-SG Global Securities Pvt., started taking calls from clients in Singapore as early as 6:30 a.m. Friday and continued fielding queries late into the day as Indian stocks rallied.“Foreign investors are suddenly pouring in,” Singh said. “I have taken more calls from foreign funds this week than I have all year,” he said. “I think we will see more inflows.”Before the latest gains, key benchmarks in India and China had ranked among the world’s worst-performing stock indexes this year through October.Going Beyond AIBeyond China and India, investors are also taking a fresh look at previously overlooked corners of Asian markets that offer value and less exposure to the AI boom.While defence and financial stocks could underperform, healthcare and consumer staples firms may get a boost, Allianz Global Investors’ chief investment officer for public markets Michael Krautzberger and strategist Liam Wash wrote in a recent note.In Korea, Fidelity’s long-only portfolio manager Dale Nicholls said he sees early signs of rotation beyond the semiconductor heavyweights, particularly among domestic pension funds.“Consumption-related areas stand out, spanning sectors from wellness through to some of the K-pop entertainment agencies” and Korea’s beauty and cosmetics industry, he said.At hedge fund ACG Management Pte., managing director Hui Ling Loh said Korea’s consumer stocks including retailers, cosmetics, food and beverage are benefiting from the perception that they are largely domestically oriented and face limited tariff and policy risks from the US.Phillip Wool, head of portfolio management at Rayliant Global Advisors, said he sees opportunity in Korea and Taiwan, “but it’s going to be beyond the highest-profile chip stocks that have run up so much and are now subject to so much unease.”One stock Wool likes is LG Electronics Inc., which he holds in his active emerging-markets exchange-traded fund. The company sells a lot of TVs, refrigerators and washing machines in the US, which “could be a catalyst for some upside as tariff pressure eases,” he said.The prospect of less isolationist US trade policies has also raised investor confidence in auto firms including Japan’s Toyota Motor Corp. and South Korea’s Hyundai Motor Co.Not everyone is ready to abandon AI. Some investors say the selloff may offer an opportunity to buy the dip, given the sector’s longer-term growth prospects.But for now, caution remains the prevalent mood.Foreigners will likely continue to sell Asia’s AI “picks and shovels” stocks, said Manishi Raychaudhuri, chief executive officer of Emmer Capital Partners Ltd. “India and China are the only two large liquid markets offering a considerable array of non-AI exposures.”

ClickPost, an AI logistics automation and post-purchase platform for D2C and retail, analysed more than 8 crore orders placed on the websites of nearly 400 D2C brands. It compared the festive shopping windows of September 20 to November 5 this year and September 1 to October 17 last year.
According to ClickPost's report, gross merchandise value (GMV), the total value of goods sold, grew about 1.7 times faster than the number of orders.
The report said this was because shoppers bought higher-priced products despite rising retail prices, rather than looking for cheaper alternatives.
Spending was concentrated in high-value categories such as luxury fashion, skincare, wellness and jewellery, it said.
Despite the higher volumes, deliveries became more reliable. .

articles.title: Emergency a mistake: Sonia Gandhi
articles.summary: New Delhi: Weighing in on the Emergency, Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has called the decision to impose it a mistake and said that she believes that her mother-in-law and then prime minister Indira Gandhi also came to feel the same.The Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson in her upcoming book "Belonging: A Journey of Love" also writes that keeping Sanjay Gandhi "in check" could have prevented much of the damage that followed the imposition of the Emergency, according to The Guardian.Also Read: Sonia Gandhi says Penguin was 'uneasy' with criticism of govtIn an interview with the British daily ahead of the launch of her memoir, Sonia Gandhi said, "I always feel that Mrs (Indira) Gandhi was a democrat at heart.""I know that many would laugh at this, but I believe she was never comfortable in the course of the emergency. I think it was sitting heavy on her," she added.Sonia Gandhi, who also holds the distinction of being the longest serving president of the Congress, was quoted by the British daily as saying that it was a mistake for Indira Gandhi to call the Emergency, and that she believes her mother-in-law came to feel the same.Also Read: 'I will carry national flag across country, even if arrested': CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke at Kochi protestAccording to Gandhi, the family was split on the decision of Emergency.Sonia Gandhi's husband Rajiv was against the move, telling his mother to wait for the next election, but her younger son Sanjay pushed for it, arguing at one family dinner that the opposition would destroy his mother and telling her, "They must be stopped", the Guardian reported.Sonia Gandhi was quoted as saying that it inflamed tensions within the family, too, as Rajiv attempted to confront his mother, but she refused to listen."Keeping Sanjay in check could have prevented much of the damage that followed," Gandhi writes in her book, according to The Guardian.In another interview published in The Hindu on Saturday ahead of the launch of her book, Gandhi has also spoken about the turbulent times of the Emergency.She said that hindsight allows people to put things better in perspective and pointed out that Indira Gandhi herself later publicly expressed regret and apologised for excesses during the Emergency.Asked about Sanjay Gandhi's name becoming synonymous with the Emergency, and whether the excesses of that time could have been avoided had Indira Gandhi listened to her elder son Rajiv and to others, Sonia Gandhi said, "It was not only Sanjay, though in the public mind he is often seen as synonymous with the Emergency. There was a lot of pressure from some of her senior colleagues, and I think there were very few people around her like Rajiv who had a different point of view.""I think eventually my mother-in-law began to understand the situation through her own wisdom and took actions to remedy it," she said."It was only after the Emergency that I came to know the true gravity of what had been happening. Yes, democratic rights had been curtailed and there was a suspension of habeas corpus, but it was done constitutionally," the former Congress chief said."Yet, when I take myself back to that period and try and see it from Mrs Gandhi's point of view, I see her struggling to cope with the rapidly deteriorating prevailing circumstances: violent protests, government offices and public transport set on fire, widespread organised unrest and even a call for the bureaucracy and armed forces to disobey orders," Gandhi said.Hindsight allows us to put things better in perspective, she said.Sonia Gandhi pointed out that Indira herself came to recognise what was happening and called for the March 1977 election."And you know very well that she herself later publicly expressed regret and apologised for excesses during the Emergency," she said.According to The Guardian, Gandhi also recalled crying as she witnessed the demolition of the Babri mosque in 1992.Gandhi knew then that they faced "a long battle for the secular nation that Mahatma Gandhi, Nehru and their colleagues had strived to build", the British daily said.She accepted that failures of her own party in part contributed to the rise of the BJP and its hardline Hindutva politics."I think we have been too complacent in many ways. There was a laissez-faire kind of an attitude," she said.Emergency was imposed by Indira Gandhi just before midnight of June 25, 1975. President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed issued the proclamation at Gandhi's behest that was later ratified by the Union Cabinet.On January 18, 1977, Indira Gandhi called for fresh elections and released all political prisoners.On March 16, 1977, Indira Gandhi and son Sanjay were defeated in Lok Sabha elections and on March 21 that year, the Emergency officially came to an end.The BJP has been criticising the Congress over the Emergency, calling it a "murder of democracy".The Modi government has been observing 'Samvidhan Hatya Diwas' to mark the "dark phase" in Indian democracy.

Delhi's AQI at 369 was in the 'very poor' category on Saturday as smog enveloped the city on the eve of Diwali and reduced visibility.
The air quality is forecast to turn 'severe' on Sunday, with Diwali celebrations, vehicular emissions and the peak stubble-burning season expected to add to the pollution burden.
Of the 59 monitoring stations that recorded data on Saturday, air quality remained in the 'severe' category for 16, while for 29, it was in the 'very poor' category. The worst AQI was recorded near IIT Delhi at 452.
The city's average AQI improved slightly from 382 on Friday to 369 on Saturday, remaining close to the 'severe' threshold of 400. Several monitoring stations have already breached this mark, indicating a deterioration in air quality across the capital city.

articles.title: Airstrike kills 22 near Yemen's capital
articles.summary: Airstrikes hit homes in a village near Yemen's capital, Sanaa, on Saturday, killing at least 22 people and wounding 30 others, mostly women and children, a spokesman for Yemen's Houthi-run Health Ministry said.Speaking to The Associated Press, Anees Alasbahi accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out the strikes on al-Shariya. The AP could not independently verify the claims, and Saudi Arabia's Information Ministry did not immediately reply to an AP request for comment.The toll reflected the rapid worsening of Yemen's civil war, where a yearslong truce fell apart over the summer. Fighting has escalated between the Iranian-backed Houthis - who control Sanaa, the north and the west of the country - and their Saudi-backed opponents based in the south and east.On Friday, an airstrike in a market in southern Yemen killed at least 30 people, according to Houthi officials. The Houthis and Yemen's Saudi-backed military each blamed the other for that strike.Footage from Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV of the aftermath of Saturday's strikes showed staff carrying limp bodies of young children out of ambulances bringing the casualties to a local hospital. One little girl's head had been cleaved open. Other children lay on stretchers, bloodied and bandaged as staff tended to them. Footage from the village showed the rubble of destroyed houses and dust filling the air as people hid in nearby agricultural fields.Alasbahi said in a posting earlier on X that Saturday's strikes hit several homes in al-Shariyah. Subsequent strikes targeted emergency responders, he told the AP.In September, the Houthis made a lightning advance capturing much of Yemen's Red Sea coast and strategic islands in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. They have also encircled the city of Taiz, a strategic gateway to southern Yemen. At the same time, they have stepped up strikes on Saudi Arabia, targeting oil and military infrastructure and shipping in the Red Sea.

articles.title: UP govt hikes DA by 5%, employees to get arrears retrospectively from Jul 1
articles.summary:
The Uttar Pradesh government has hiked the Dearness Allowance (DA) by 5 per cent for state government employees, staff in aided educational and technical institutions, regular and full-time employees of urban local bodies, work-charged employees, and those serving on UGC pay scales.
Employees will now receive a Dearness Allowance of 63 per cent, up from 58 per cent. The increased rate will be effective from July 1, 2026, the state government said in a statement on Saturday.
A government order was also issued in this regard on Saturday.
The enhanced dearness allowance will be paid along with the regular salary for November 2026. This government decision will benefit lakhs of employees across the state.
The move by the Yogi Adityanath government will provide relief not only to the state's regular employees but also to staff in aided educational institutions, urban local bodies, and other eligible categories of employees, the statement said.

It earlier announced a ban on the plying of non-Delhi-registered motor vehicles that are below BS-VI emission norms for the same period this year -- which is usually marked by the worst of the city's air pollution and quality -- under its Winter Action Plan to limit vehicular emissions and curb dust on roads.
"Every year, from November 1 to January 31, other state-registered BS-IV and below vehicles will not be allowed to ply in Delhi," a Delhi transport department's public notification said on Saturday.

articles.title: Centre allows transfer of prisoners between Chandigarh, other states
articles.summary:
The Centre has extended the Punjab Police and Correctional Services Act, 2006, to the Union Territory of Chandigarh, introducing provisions for the transfer of prisoners between states and Union territories and changes to the functioning of the prison administration.
The notification, issued under Section 87 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, extends the Punjab legislation to the Union Territory of Chandigarh with certain modifications, according to a notification issued by the Union Home Ministry on Friday.
The amended provisions deal with the transfer of prisoners between Chandigarh and other states or Union territories.
Under the provisions, prisoners serving sentences in Chandigarh, including life imprisonment, may be transferred to prisons in another state or Union territory with the consent of the government concerned and an order issued by the Chandigarh administrator.
The amendments also provide for the transfer of undertrial prisoners in the interest of Chandigarh's .

articles.title: Illegal US migration: Indians remain in top 3
articles.summary: Indian nationals continued to rank as the third-largest group encountered by US border authorities in the 2026 fiscal year, despite a steep decline in illegal migration attempts following President Donald Trump's crackdown on unauthorised immigration.US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) data show that 30,528 Indian nationals were encountered by border authorities in FY26, which ran from October 2025 to September 2026. Only Mexican and Canadian nationals recorded higher numbers, with 1,23,439 and 37,700 encounters, respectively.India ranked ahead of China, which recorded 29,818 encounters. The figures indicate that attempts by Indians to enter the US illegally continue despite tougher enforcement and the risks associated with the journey, commonly known as the 'donkey route'.According to sources familiar with illegal immigration networks, a sizeable number of those attempting the journey are from Gujarat, Punjab and Andhra Pradesh. Within Gujarat, people from North and Central Gujarat continue to figure prominently among those seeking to enter the US through unauthorised routes.Illegal migration encounters from India fall nearly 64%135630363The number of Indian nationals encountered at US borders has declined considerably over the past three fiscal years. US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) recorded 90,415 encounters involving Indians in FY24. This fell to 34,146 in FY25 and further to 30,528 in FY26, marking a decline of nearly 64% from FY24.The reduction coincides with the Trump administration's tougher immigration enforcement measures. Trump returned to the White House on January 20, 2025, after winning the November 2024 presidential election, with a crackdown on illegal immigration among his administration's major priorities.The decline in Indian encounters is part of a wider fall in unauthorised migration to the US. CBP recorded 3,82,490 border encounters across nationalities in FY26, nearly 45% below the 6,91,906 recorded in FY25. The corresponding figures were considerably higher in FY24 and FY23, at around 29 lakh and 32 lakh, respectively.Among other nationalities, Guatemala accounted for 18,319 encounters, followed by the Philippines with 17,985 and Honduras with 13,005. Brazil recorded 6,285, Russia 5,327 and Venezuela 4,945. Nationals of other countries, grouped, accounted for 63,678 encounters.Gujarat continues to bear the human cost135630381The continuing attempts to reach the US illegally have also resulted in fatalities and disappearances. At least 11 people from Gujarat died and another 11 were injured or went missing between 2022 and 2025 while attempting the journey.One of the most devastating incidents occurred on January 19, 2022, when four members of a family from Dingucha village in Gujarat's Gandhinagar district froze to death near the US-Canada border. Jagdish Patel, 30, his wife Vaishali, 37, and their children Vihang, 13, and Dharmik, aged three, were found dead near Emerson in Manitoba, Canada, around 10 metres from the border. The family had been travelling on foot when they were caught in a blizzard.On March 28, 2023, four members of a family from Manekpura village in Mehsana district drowned after a boat capsized. Another tragedy occurred on May 5, 2025, when two children from Mehsana drowned off the California coast.Despite these incidents, illegal migration networks continue to attract people with the promise of better financial prospects in the US.A source familiar with the networks said, "Though people have been shunted out of the US through Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) crackdown, a large number of Gujaratis mainly from North and Central Gujarat are sneaking into America for better financial security."The source added that attempts to enter through the Mexican and Canadian borders were continuing, with individuals reportedly paying between Rs 80 lakh and Rs 1.25 crore for the journey.- Reference taken from TOI

According to Samco Securities, the current market environment presents an opportunity for investors to increase their exposure to equities in Samvat 2083, while retaining existing gold investments as a portfolio hedge.In its Market Outlook for Samvat 2083, the brokerage highlighted that the Sensex-to-Gold ratio currently stands at 6.43, significantly below its long-term median of 9.8 since 1990. The ratio is also lower than approximately 86% of its monthly readings over the period.The ratio had touched 5.26 in March 2026, its lowest level since 1991, reflecting the extent of Indian equities' underperformance against gold during the recent market cycle.Historically, similar levels have marked attractive entry points for equity investors. The ratio previously entered comparable territory in 1993, 2001-03, 2009 and 2011-13. On each of these occasions, Indian equities subsequently outperformed gold by a significant margin over the following years.“Relative to gold, Indian stocks are as cheap as they have been in a generation. Gold has done its job as a hedge, and we recommend holding on to existing gold investments but not adding to them aggressively at these levels,” said the brokerage in its report.135629914The brokerage further believes the current valuation gap provides an opportunity to increase equity exposure. "This is the time to tilt your portfolio towards equities," it recommended, while advising investors to retain their existing gold investments rather than aggressively adding to them at current levels.Why Samco believes equities could outperform goldThe Sensex-to-Gold ratio provides a broader perspective on investor sentiment and relative asset performance. A rising ratio indicates that equities are outperforming gold and investors are increasingly willing to take risks. A declining ratio, on the other hand, suggests a preference for gold and safer assets.Samco noted that the decline in the ratio during the previous Samvat was initially driven largely by the rally in gold rather than a collapse in equities. However, Samvat 2082 brought the equity correction that the brokerage had considered necessary for a more durable bottom.During the period, the Sensex declined from its high of 85,762 to a low of 71,593, while gold continued to advance, pushing the ratio to its March 2026 trough of 5.26.With the ratio now recovering to 6.43, Samco believes the relative valuation equation favours equities.Cheap valuations, but global risks remainDespite its constructive outlook on equities, Samco has cautioned that the risks confronting Indian markets have not disappeared.Elevated crude oil prices, currency depreciation and global market volatility remain important considerations for investors entering Samvat 2083.Brent crude remained above $100 for much of the year amid the US-Iran conflict. Given India's dependence on crude oil imports, sustained high prices could put pressure on the rupee, inflation, government finances and corporate profit margins.Currency weakness is another concern. The rupee depreciated from 87.88 to 95.15 against the US dollar during the Samvat, a decline of approximately 8%, and touched record lows near 97. Persistent foreign investor outflows and a wide trade deficit continue to weigh on the domestic currency.Global market leadership has also shifted, with US healthcare, energy and financial stocks gaining prominence over technology and semiconductor stocks. Volatility across asset classes remains elevated."Cheap valuations tell us what to own; uncertainty tells us how to own it," Samco said, outlining diversification as its preferred strategy for the year ahead.Samco's stock picks for Samvat 2083Against this backdrop, Samco has identified a diversified basket of Indian stocks across sectors and investment horizons, combining long-term growth opportunities with shorter-term tactical ideas.Among the one-year recommendations, Adani Power represents the power-generation theme, while BSE offers exposure to the growing capital-market infrastructure segment. Tech Mahindra is positioned as a potential turnaround and rupee beneficiary.Azad Engineering and HFCL feature as high-growth opportunities linked to aerospace, defence, energy components, telecom and data-centre connectivity. Tips Music, meanwhile, represents an asset-light business model in the media and entertainment space.For the six-month investment horizon, Samco has selected L&T Technology Services, citing the potential for an earnings recovery and benefits from rupee depreciation, alongside TVS Motor Company as a consumption-oriented opportunity.The shorter-term basket includes MCX, which could benefit from increased market volatility, and Sansera Engineering, which features as a momentum-oriented play in the auto and aerospace components space.135629881Why US ETFs find a place in Samco's portfolioA notable feature of Samco's strategy for Samvat 2083 is its recommendation to diversify beyond Indian equities through dollar-denominated US-listed exchange-traded funds (ETFs).The brokerage has identified two ETFs: the Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) and the Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLV).The XLE ETF provides exposure to the US energy sector and is positioned as a potential hedge against rising crude oil prices. This is particularly relevant for Indian investors because higher oil prices can hurt domestic equities through their impact on import costs, inflation and the rupee.The XLV ETF, which tracks the US healthcare sector, is recommended as a defensive, dollar-denominated holding that could help cushion portfolios against further weakness in the Indian currency.Indian investors should consider geographical diversificationSamco's overseas allocation strategy is built around three considerations: currency diversification, access to global businesses and the potential benefits of lower correlation between markets.For Indian investors with future expenses linked to foreign currencies, including overseas education and travel, holding dollar-denominated assets can help protect purchasing power when the rupee depreciates.US markets also provide access to global leaders in sectors such as technology, healthcare and energy, where comparable investment opportunities may not always be available in the domestic market.The brokerage also pointed out that Indian and US equities do not necessarily move in tandem. During Samvat 2082, the S&P 500 gained while the Nifty declined, illustrating the diversification benefits of holding assets across markets.Resident Indian individuals can invest overseas under the Reserve Bank of India's Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS). However, returns from US investments depend on both the underlying security's performance in dollar terms and movements in the USD/INR exchange rate.Disclosure: This article has been written by Kumar Gaurav, who is not a Sebi-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. Jubilant delivery growth lifts Domino's India
articles.summary: Jubilant FoodWorks, which operates Domino's Pizza and Popeyes in India, reported strong growth in its delivery business in the September quarter, while Popeyes continued to gain traction, emerging as a second growth engine for the quick-service restaurant (QSR) operator.Domino's India reported a 9.2% year-on-year increase in revenue in Q2 FY27, supported by 6.3% growth in orders. Revenue from its delivery channel grew 11.3% during the quarter, with delivery accounting for 75.8% of the brand's total revenue. The company's like-for-like (LFL) growth improved to 4.1% from 2.5% in the June quarter and 0.2% in the March quarter.Also read: Diwali shopping gets costlier this year: From milk, ghee, butter to dry fruits135628398The QSR giant reported sustained momentum in delivery, along with early signs of recovery in its dine-in and takeaway (DITA) business, supported the improvement in Domino's India performance. Late-night consumption also emerged as a strong-performing segment, with more than 90% of the network now offering services until 3 am.Over the past six to nine months, the company has expanded its late-night offerings to tap into additional consumption occasions and drive incremental orders. Product launches across the Maxxx range, Double Cheese Burst, cold coffee and mousse have also helped improve customer engagement and average ticket sizes.The company is also working to revive its dine-in and takeaway business, which recorded 2.4% revenue growth during the quarter. Infrastructure upgrades have been completed in around 20% of the identified stores, while its My Meal at Rs 119 proposition has been rolled out nationally to drive footfalls and improve ticket sizes.Meanwhile, Popeyes is gaining scale and emerging as a meaningful second growth engine for Jubilant FoodWorks. The fried chicken chain reported 122% year-on-year revenue growth in Q2 FY27, with like-for-like growth of 53%, marking its fourth consecutive quarter of growth above 40%.Also read: Quick commerce emerges beyond Diwali shopping panic to breathe on the necks of e-commerce giantsPopeyes added 11 stores during the quarter, taking its presence to 25 cities. Its system-level average daily sales are now broadly comparable with established competitors in most markets, according to the company.The brand's growth has also been accompanied by an improvement in profitability. Popeyes' gross margin expanded by 150 basis points year-on-year during the quarter. Jubilant FoodWorks is targeting the development of Popeyes into a Rs 1,000 crore brand over the next three to four years.However, the company is prioritising store-level returns and unit economics over an aggressive expansion strategy. While customer experience, gross margins and store productivity are approaching or matching competitive benchmarks, brand-level profitability is not yet fully established.Jubilant FoodWorks said it was following the expansion strategy adopted for Domino's, focusing on entering the right micro-markets, maintaining attractive store-level economics and ensuring new outlets meet return thresholds before accelerating expansion.At the consolidated level, Jubilant FoodWorks reported an 11.8% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 2,608 crore in Q2 FY27. EBITDA rose 7.3% to Rs 513 crore. Standalone revenue grew 11.5% to Rs 1,885 crore, while EBITDA increased 12.4% to Rs 372 crore.The company added 108 stores across its businesses during the quarter, taking its global network to 3,820 outlets.The Domino's India franchisee is managing elevated input costs through procurement efficiencies, calibrated pricing, menu-mix optimisation and tighter cost controls. Its standalone gross margin expanded 110 basis points year-on-year to 75.5%, while standalone EBITDA margin improved 16 basis points to 19.8%.The company is prioritising sustained growth at Domino's India, scaling Popeyes while improving unit economics, developing its international businesses and embedding technology across operations.

articles.title: China's giant pandas make debut at US zoo
articles.summary: Atlanta: Giant pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang delighted visitors to Zoo Atlanta during their public debut Friday, chewing bamboo and lounging in their new US habitat while on loan from China.A male named Ping Ping and female Fu Shuang arrived from Chengdu in September via a FedEx flight dubbed the "Panda Express," and are to be hosted in the southern US facility for the next 10 years.Pandas are "animals that have got a unique ability to inspire curiosity, instill passion, evoke joy, and unite people around the globe," CEO Raymond King told onlookers at Zoo Atlanta."This extraordinary spirit of partnership helps create a future for a species that is truly beloved the world over."In preparation for their arrival, Zoo Atlanta has renovated its panda facilities and assembled a team of animal caretakers.It has also ensured a stable and long-term supply of bamboo, grown locally in Atlanta, which has a climate that is very similar to Chengdu."I think they inspire happiness," zoo visitor Rachel Totts told AFP on Friday. "They make people smile. I've never seen someone not say 'Oh, it's so cute!' when they're looking at a panda."Soft, furry power Native to temperate forest habitats in East Asia, the lumbering black-and-white mammals do not typically travel long distances in the wild.But many have been shipped to zoos around the world as apart of Beijing's decades-long "panda diplomacy" program to foster foreign ties.The furry show of "soft power" came as top US officials on Friday called on China to uphold the trade agreement made in an October 2025 meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping.The accord calmed tensions after a whirlwind of tariff hikes, and required China to buy US soybeans while suspending export controls on rare earths.Before 2016 pandas were considered endangered but are now listed as "vulnerable" by wildlife advocates, and an estimated 1,800 pandas live in the wild.The Chinese government has established more than 50 panda reserves for conservation, but in the wild the bears continue to face threats of habitat loss and poaching.Panda pairs Atlanta previously hosted pandas on loan from China starting in 1999, and seven panda cubs have been born at the zoo. All are now back in Chengdu, and Zoo Atlanta has not had any pandas since 2024.Atlanta native John Perez celebrated his 28th birthday at Zoo Atlanta on Friday, telling AFP the pandas drew him to visit for the first time because "it felt perfect, you know?"Both of the new arrivals were born in 2020, and it's hoped they will be suitable mates. Pandas in captivity typically live for around 30 years.In 1972, China gifted a pair of pandas to Washington, following US president Richard Nixon's historic visit to the Communist nation.Beijing recalled two of its pandas from Japan early this year, following a diplomatic spat that began when Japan's prime minister hinted that Tokyo could intervene militarily in the event of any attack on Taiwan.

EU's 2030 move puts single-use sachets in focus
articles.summary: Now, over 70 years since they were invented, single-serve tomato ketchup sachets are slated to become contraband from 2030 under the European Union's Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation. Maybe in the future, secret stashes of them will find their way on to the dark web (or its future equivalent) to be picked up for a fortune by collectors and hoarded away in airtight vaults. Even further in the future, they will be unearthed as 20th century material culture.A newly rekindled romance with Europe has seen the current Labour-led British government there become willin', Barkis-like, to adopt rules that routinely used to make their Conservative predecessors see red. And that has now led to talk of an outrageous assault on a familiar and beloved table accessory in countless British pubs and eateries: sachets of not only single-serve ketchup but also mayonnaise, mustard and vinegar, usually reposing in a convenient bowl.Also Read: Why best leaders don't try to save the worldNo doubt back in 1955, Messrs Harold Ross and Yale Kaplan did yeoman service to the food trade by apportioning the right amount of condiment and ensconcing it in a sachet that required less energy to open and dispense than bottles or jars. Bigger receptacles were messy and wasteful it was believed, and sachets offered a clean and ordered - read, pre-measured - alternative that required no thought. Clearly, they had read the average convenience junkie's mind perfectly.Of course, the primary beneficiary of these prepackaged condiments were eateries themselves. Which business would not want to obviate the chance of wasteful or butter-fingered customers dispensing more from bottles than necessary? The extra packing cost per unit of ketchup is recouped by lower wastage even though the sachets are offered "free". Not many such sachets go waste anyway, even if a few brazen types grab handfuls of each to go with their fish and chips.Few humans can resist the allure of those sauce packets in our current stage of evolution. This writer included. When any of those come in my standard airline meal, I sagely tuck them into my bag rather than hand them back unopened along with my empty tray to the cabin crew. Ditto for wet tissue sachets, sugar packets, miniature jam and butter tubs and small water bottles. Is that wastage or thriftiness on my part? All my travel bags have a few tucked away from last time...Single-use sachets have become all pervasive in India, from pickles to shampoo, biscuits to spices, ointments to detergents. Speaking anecdotally, though, pan masala and gutka sachets appear to be the most pernicious. Those shiny, empty sachets find their way into every nook and cranny; most disturbingly they turn up even in the garden soil when I am repotting a plant. Millions of thoughtlessly chucked sachets now clog up our water bodies, forests and farmlands.Our planet would be better off without all sachets, but this EU regulation exempts takeaway food. So those ubiquitous oregano and chilli flakes sachets that arrive with pizza and burger orders will still be available for stockpiling by human packrats after 2030. Hospitals and nursing homes will also be exempt, on grounds of hygiene and safety. EU being EU, alternatives are also helpfully listed: refillable sauce dispensers, small bowls for jam and jugs for creamers.The EU regulation is aimed only at establishments that provide these to those who dine in. But there is a case to draw a line under this brilliant 20th century invention - for the sake of future centuries. Pre-portioned packaging really underestimates humans: we can go to the moon and deep space but cannot use a squeezy jar or a bottle at a fast-food restaurant or at home for ketchup or mustard? Single-use plastics are the most dispensable of inventions, pun intended.

articles.title: Airtel calls for industry-wide data pricing reset
articles.summary: New Delhi: Bharti Airtel Friday told analysts its prepaid tweaks are only a trial run, and that sustained growth in average revenue per user - a key growth metric - will need a sector-wide shift in how data is priced.Asked on the Q2 FY27 earnings call whether its August intervention was a step towards fixing the industry's pricing architecture, Shashwat Sharma, managing director of Bharti Airtel, said the problem was structural. The sector, he said, has "a very flat architecture and very low ARPUs.""You're giving away unlimited usage, and you're not monetising consumption in a way. Data in that sense is not charged properly." The withdrawal of the ₹299 plan move, he said, was "more of an experimentation on our own base to keep moving ARPUs up," while "the architecture correction is a much broader correction that is required in the industry."Airtel's India mobile ARPU rose to ₹271 from ₹264, helped by premiumisation and an extra day in the quarter. Sharma said the Q2 prepaid action had "already kind of paid out," with postpaid upgrades, international roaming and top-ups as the next levers.Data usage per user, an analyst noted, is closing the gap with peers to 20-odd percent. Sharma said heavy users must contribute more, "People who consume heavily must pay for data proportionately, and that is the shift the industry eventually will have to make." Doing so would give "organic growth of ARPU, which is consumption-led," and "a pivotal shift that we need to make."Sharma attributed higher churn to seasonality and tariff actions, which bring "a temporary impact on customer continuity." Interestingly, Airtel reintroduced the ₹299 plan that it had withdrawn in August, which had effectively increased the entry price for daily data plans to ₹349.

articles.title: NY Fed's John Williams flags need to gather more information on inflation risks before rate decisions
articles.summary: Federal Reserve officials are weighing the inflationary risks from strong economic activity and the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure, even as they signal the need for more data before determining the next steps on interest rates, Bloomberg reported.For live updates on US Markets, click here New York Fed President John Williams said inflation remained too high, although other indicators were not yet pointing to broader concerns. Speaking at an event hosted by the European Central Bank in Frankfurt on Friday, he backed the Fed's position that policymakers should gather more information before deciding the appropriate course for monetary policy."Inflation is absolutely too high," Williams said, while noting that wage growth remained consistent with the central bank's 2% inflation target and inflation expectations were well anchored.Fed weighs inflation against economic resilienceWilliams said monetary policy had an important role in preventing temporary price shocks from spreading into broader or more persistent inflation.Also Read: Federal Reserve rate hike bets strengthen as US jobs growth beats estimates"Our FOMC statement last meeting, I think, captures correctly that this is an appropriate time to accumulate more information to help us determine what the appropriate stance of policy is to make make sure we achieve a timely return to our 2% target," he said, according to the Bloomberg report.The Fed held interest rates steady at its previous meeting after raising its benchmark rate by 25 basis points in September to a range of 3.75%-4%. Policymakers have since emphasised the need for additional information while keeping the possibility of further rate increases open, Bloomberg reported.The central bank's preferred inflation gauge, the personal consumption expenditures price index, rose 3.6% in September from a year earlier. Underlying inflation measures that exclude food and energy also increased. Meanwhile, the US economy expanded at its fastest pace in a year in the quarter ended September.AI infrastructure raises fresh inflation concernsSeparately, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem warned that the rapid build-out of AI infrastructure could add to near-term inflationary pressures, Bloomberg reported."When I look at inflation, excess inflation today, it’s coming both from negative supply shocks related to the Middle East and demand forces coming related to the AI build," Musalem said.While acknowledging AI's potential to improve productivity over time, he cautioned against shaping current monetary policy around benefits that may take years to materialise."We need to make monetary policy for the economy of the day," he said. "We cannot make monetary policy for the economy as it may be five years from now."(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.summary: The Federal Reserve's case for another interest rate hike in December has gained momentum after stronger than expected US employment data reinforced signs of economic resilience, shifting attention back to persistent inflation from concerns over a potential AI driven slowdown, Reuters reported.US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, more than double the 65,000 expected by economists, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The unemployment rate also edged down to 4.1%, suggesting the labour market remains firm despite concerns over the economic outlook.For live updates on US Markets, click here Following the report, markets priced in an 85% probability of a quarter point rate increase at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting, up from around 75% before the data release. Traders also brought forward expectations of another rate increase to April from June, Reuters reported.Strong jobs data reinforce Fed's hawkish outlookThe employment figures strengthen the argument for further monetary tightening as the Fed continues to battle inflation, which has remained above its 2% target for more than five years.Also Read: Nasdaq rebounds as chip stocks recover from steep losses, rate fears persist"This is a very strong labor market report on the heels of solid GDP and consumer spending data last week, reinforcing the economy’s positive momentum," Fitch Ratings analyst Olu Sonola wrote after the release.While acknowledging the risks posed by recent AI related concerns, Sonola said the economy remained on firm footing and that labour market resilience was pushing the policy debate towards a December rate hike, Reuters reported.Raymond James analysts also expect the central bank to raise rates next month."For the Federal Reserve, this should allow them to concentrate on the inflation side of their mandate," the analysts wrote. "We expect the Fed to increase the federal funds rate by 25 basis points in December."AI concerns had clouded rate outlookExpectations of another rate increase had weakened after Democrats' midterm election gains raised concerns about tighter regulation of AI and data centre construction.The prospect of slower AI investment had fuelled worries about weaker economic growth and easing inflationary pressures, reducing the urgency for further monetary tightening.However, Friday's employment report has renewed expectations that the Fed will prioritise inflation control as it assesses the strength of the US economy.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.title: FIIs step up India buying, pour Rs 13,750 crore on Friday; total buying hits Rs 53,154 crore in 14 days
articles.summary: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) stepped up their buying in Indian equities on Friday, November 6, pumping in a net Rs 13,750 crore and extending their buying streak to 14 trading sessions. With the latest purchase, cumulative FII investments since October 16 have reached Rs 53,154 crore, according to the exchange data.Friday's buying followed another massive investment of Rs 14,975 crore on Thursday, November 5, marking the biggest single-day FII purchase in Indian equities in more than a year.The pace of foreign buying has accelerated in recent sessions, with FIIs investing a net Rs 34,584 crore over the past five trading sessions alone. The latest inflows mark a sharp turnaround from the prolonged selling witnessed earlier this year, when overseas investors withdrew billions of dollars from Indian equities.The foreign buying came even as domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued to sell. DIIs offloaded shares worth a net Rs 5,969 crore on Friday, following net sales of Rs 10,445 crore in the previous session. Their combined net selling over the two sessions stood at Rs 16,414 crore.The return of foreign buying follows months of sustained selling amid elevated crude oil prices, geopolitical tensions in West Asia, a weakening rupee and concerns over corporate earnings.Foreign selling intensified in September and October as oil prices climbed and global investors reduced their exposure to emerging markets. The outflows had pushed foreign ownership of Indian equities to historic lows.Global brokerage Nomura said Indian equities could become more attractive to foreign investors as earnings improve and valuations remain below their post-pandemic averages. It also noted that the correction in artificial intelligence-related stocks in international markets could encourage investors to redirect capital towards other markets, including India.Expectations of a possible reduction in long-term capital gains tax for foreign investors have also added to optimism, although any such change remains uncertain.ALSO READ: $5 billion in 5 days! Why FIIs are suddenly shopping Indian stocks non-stop this DiwaliSensex, Nifty climb higherIndian equities defied a global sell-off on Friday, extending their winning streak as investors turned to domestic markets as a relative safe haven amid turmoil across global markets. The Nifty 50 surged 494 points, or 2.01%, to settle at 25,030, while the BSE Sensex advanced 1,718 points, or 2.17%, to close at 81,028.The broader markets, however, came under pressure. The Nifty Smallcap 250 declined 0.85%, while the Nifty Midcap 100 ended marginally lower, signalling continued weakness beyond the benchmark indices.Among sectoral indices, the Nifty Private Bank index led the gains, rallying more than 3%, while the Nifty Financial Services index advanced over 2.5%. The Nifty Consumer Durables index also gained around 2%.Despite the sharp gains in benchmark indices, market volatility remained elevated. Bucking the trend, Asian Paints, Bajaj Finance and Power Grid shares dropped more than 2% each to lead losses on the benchmark index.Also read | Infosys, Wipro, TCS and other IT stocks rise up to 3% amid US AI rout; is the bubble bursting?While benchmark indices extended gains, broader markets however, crashed. Nifty Smallcap 250 index plunged nearly 2% while Nifty Midcap 100 index dropped more than 1% on Friday morning. As a result, the overall market breadth turned negative, with NSE seeing 2,236 declines against 824 advances, while 94 stocks remained unchanged.Among the sectors, Nifty Metal plunged more than 2% to lead losses, while Nifty IT gained 1.5% to lead gains. India VIX, which measures volatility in the market, soared nearly 7% to near 17.What lies ahead for Dalal Street?The blood bath in the US markets will impact most other markets today, but India is likely to be the least impacted, said V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments. He noted that the big rout of 5.6% in Nasdaq was triggered on concerns of a big slowdown in data centre spending since the Democrats are opposed to massive data centre investment. This tech rout, particularly the sharp deceleration in AI trade will turn out to be beneficial for India, according to the analyst.“It is important to note that the FIIs have bought equities for Rs 35781 crores in the last five trading days. articles.title: Infosys, Wipro, TCS and other IT stocks rise up to 3% amid US AI rout; is the bubble bursting?
articles.summary: The shares of Indian IT companies, including Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro and others, rose up to 3% on Friday even as the global AI selloff intensified sharply, with Wall Street seeing its worst crash since 2020, boosting sentiment for the Indian IT stocks, which are seen to have the so-called ‘anti-AI’ advantage.In today's session, Infosys gained over 2%, while India's biggest IT company, TCS, rose 3% to Rs 2,565 per share. Wipro, HCL Tech, Coforge, and Persistent Systems gained up to 2% after the opening bell.Artificial intelligence-linked stocks plunged on fears of tougher AI regulation after Democrats won ‌control of the US Congress, defeating President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the midterm elections. Democrats’ victory sparked concerns that tighter regulation could slow the AI infrastructure buildout that has helped lift stocks to record highs this year.Nasdaq fell 6%, marking its worst drop since the infamous Covid-19 crash in March 2020. The tech-heavy index also entered a technical ‘correction’ territory, a 10% drop from ⁠its October 6 record-high close.Nvidia shares plunged more than 9%, while the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index crashed over 12%. The selloff wiped off $3 trillion in stock market value from S&P 500 companies. South Korea’s Kospi, which was seen as the face of the sharp volatility around the AI frenzy, also felt the pain, crashing more than 9% to trigger a circuit breaker.Also read | US stocks suffer worst rout since 2020: Dow plunges 1,800 points, Nasdaq crashes 5.5% as AI fears wipe out $3 trillion"Investors appear to be recognizing that some newly elected members of Congress and governors are looking to slow the pace of AI infrastructure development," Reuters quoted Melissa Brown, global head of investment decision research at SimCorp."While it seems unlikely that they will be able to stop it altogether, any slowdown would raise concerns because the AI growth story has largely depended on the rapid buildout of supporting infrastructure,” she said.Why Indian IT stocks stand to benefitEarlier this year, when Anthropic’s launch of new plugins for Claude triggered sharp hopes for artificial intelligence, India’s much-touted IT services companies saw a massive rout in their share prices as analysts worried that innovations could lead to displacement in the sector. "We call it the ‘SaaSpocalypse,’ an apocalypse for software-as-a-service stocks," Bloomberg quoted Jeffrey Favuzza from the equity trading desk at Jefferies as saying.However, as the AI frenzy began to fizzle out, analysts were quick to point out India’s so-called ‘anti-AI’ advantage. This has been boosting a recovery in these stocks while experts scream about a bubble-burst crisis ahead amid the massive spending behind AI infrastructure. Michael Burry, popular for correctly predicting the 2008 housing crisis, has been ramping up his warnings over the excessive optimism regarding AI. Recently, he said that the market is currently in a 'denial' mood, a phase that could last six to nine months as seen during the previous 2000 and 2008 crises.Also read | AI bubble is coming, and there is no way out! Aswath Damodaran explains what investors should do before the crash beginsAmid the growing concerns over the excessive frenzy around artificial intelligence, valuation expert Ashwath Damodaran said in a recent podcast that the AI bubble is coming and there is no way one can avoid it completely.These rising worries around the AI bubble will likely be a positive for Indian IT companies. Veteran banker Uday Kotak expects India to benefit from the reverse flows as the AI frenzy fizzles out, while working down the path of building its own AI capabilities. This comes as worries around excessive spending by hyperscalers on artificial intelligence grow louder, with several analysts warning of a bubble-burst situation ahead.Also read | Uday Kotak says $700 bn outstanding FII payments will boost market, sees AI worries driving flows to IndiaDisclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. articles.summary: DUBAI, - Iran has sent the United States a nuclear proposal via Qatar, to be discussed only after Washington meets Tehran's seven demands, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Thursday.The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the US was reviewing the proposal but declined to provide further details.Mediators have intensified efforts to end the war between Iran and the United States amid fears it could reignite after the US midterm elections, with Trump on Tuesday declining to rule out a resumption of combat operations after the vote and Iran planning wider retaliation if war resumes.Iran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei had said earlier on Thursday, during a visit to Russia: "On the issue of diplomacy, we have announced seven conditions to the Americans. As long as they do not execute our seven conditions, we will neither open the Strait of Hormuz nor have negotiations".Iran has demanded the lifting of US sanctions, the release of frozen Iranian assets and war reparations, among other conditions, while Washington has said nuclear issues must be part of any initial negotiations.The US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, and Iran responded with strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. articles.title: Nithya Raman elected Mayor of Los Angeles
articles.summary: New York: Indian-born democratic socialist Nithya Raman has been elected Mayor of Los Angeles, scripting history as she becomes the first South Asian mayor of the nation's second-largest city.Raman, 45, who was a Los Angeles City Council member, defeated incumbent 73-year-old Karen Bass in the November 3 mid-term elections.Also read: Democrats' US midterm sweep may give India more room to negotiate a balanced trade deal with TrumpWith this victory, America's two largest cities - New York and Los Angeles - are now run by Indian-descent mayors who are Democratic Socialists."Los Angeles, I am deeply honoured to be your next Mayor. Thank you to the thousands of people who knocked on doors, sent texts, made phone calls, convinced their neighbours to believe in the promise of this big, beautiful, joyful city that we get to call home," Raman said in a video posted on X Thursday.Raman paid tribute to her predecessor Bass, the first woman mayor of Los Angeles, for her decades-long public service."I am going to City Hall to work every single day to earn your trust and to earn your trust in this city again. And that work starts now, so that we can build housing that people can afford, parks for our children to play in, a transit system that can get people where they need to go, a city that is safe for its working people and its families, and a city government that is actually capable of delivering on its promises," Raman said.LA City Councilmember for District 4, Kerala-born Raman is an urban planner by training, and she received her bachelor's degree from Harvard and a graduate degree from MIT.Raman is among the several Indian-American candidates who have emerged victorious across the country in the US midterm elections that concluded Tuesday and delivered a significant rebuke to President Donald Trump and the Republicans as the Democrats gained control of the House and Senate, flipping seats and traditional party strongholds in a massive blue wave across America.Also read: Marco Rubio weighs leaving administration after GOP’s midterm lossIndian American Impact, an organisation that empowers South Asian and Indian-American communities through community engagement, civic partnerships, and candidate support, congratulated Raman on her victory in the general election for Mayor of Los Angeles.Noting that Raman will become the first South Asian American mayor of the nation's second-largest city, the Indian American Impact said her victory reflects the growing political power of South Asian Americans in California, a state with more than one million South Asian residents, the largest such population in the country.Executive Director of Indian American Impact Chintan Patel said in a statement that Raman ran on lowering rents, building housing faster, and making city services work for Angelenos, and voters chose her to deliver it."With her win, South Asian Americans will lead the two largest cities in the United States," Patel said, referring to New York and its Mayor Mamdani.The 5.5 million-strong Indian-American community registered significant political gains in the midterms, with several candidates from the community winning historic elections to various positions across the country.Pia Dandiya of Florida and Dr Amish Shah of Arizona will be the newest Indian-American members of the US Congress, with their victories speaking to the "growing political power of our communities."They will join Representative Ami Bera, Representative Pramila Jayapal, Representative Ro Khanna and Representative Suhas Subramanyam at Capitol Hill."At a time of rising hate against our communities, representation matters, and they will fight to keep our communities safe," Indian American Impact said. "All six are committed to lowering costs for working families, expanding access to health care, and protecting immigrants, and they will serve as a powerful check on the Trump administration in the next Congress," the organisation said.Among the other notable election victories are that of Manoj Chourasia, who has been reelected to the New Hampshire State House, Darshana Patel who won her reelection to the California State Assembly, Ranjeev Puri whose won reelection to the Michigan House of Representatives.With Democrats retaking the chamber, Puri is expected to become Michigan's next Speaker of the House, which would make him the first Indian American Speaker of a state House in the country.Dr Krish Subrahmanian won his election for the Minnesota State Senate; Aruna Miller has been reelected as Lieutenant Governor of Maryland; Lisa Kaul won her election for the New York State Senate, defeating a Republican incumbent and flipping a seat in New York; and Nabeela Syed won her election for Illinois State Senate District 26.Amar Mukunda won his election to the Maryland State Senate; Saba Haider has been elected to the Illinois State House; Josh Kaul has been re-elected as Wisconsin's Attorney General; Pooja Sethi won her election to the Texas House, District 47, becoming the first Indian American to serve in the Texas legislature; and Jyot Singh has been elected to the Georgia State House, District 97, the first Indian American and first Sikh American elected to the Georgia State Legislature.

M-cap of BSE-listed companies tops Rs 500 lakh crore mark
articles.summary: Mumbai: The combined market capitalisation of all companies listed on the BSE crossed ₹500 lakh crore for the first time Thursday, reaching around ₹502 lakh crore ($5.31 trillion) amid a broad-based rally in equities and a steady addition of newly listed companies.It took 622 trading sessions for the total mcap to rise from ₹400 lakh crore, first crossed on April 8, 2024, to the latest milestone. The mcap first crossed ₹100 lakh crore on March 12, 2014, and took 1,494 sessions to reach ₹200 lakh crore on February 4, 2021. The ₹300 lakh crore milestone was reached on July 6, 2023, after another 586 sessions, while the subsequent rise to ₹400 lakh crore took 181 sessions.135589318The latest milestone is significant because it comes even as the benchmark Sensex and several broader market indices remain below their record highs. The Sensex is still 7.6% below its peak of 85,836, recorded on September 26, 2024.The BSE MidCap 150 is 5.3% below its record of 17,373, reached on August 26, 2026, while the BSE SmallCap 250 is 8.4% below its peak of 7,514, recorded on September 23, 2024. The BSE MicroCap 250 is 7% below its record of 19,988, reached on September 8, 2026.Read more: Why Nithin Kamath believes NRI investing in India has become easier than everA steady stream of initial public offerings (IPOs) has also contributed to the expansion of the overall mcap, even as several benchmark indices remain below their peaks. In 2024, 94 companies made their mainboard debut, adding around ₹12 lakh crore to mcap on their listing days. In 2025, 115 companies listed, adding nearly ₹14 lakh crore, while 107 companies have listed so far in 2026, adding above ₹25 lakh crore."The large number of IPOs has added to the overall mcap. At the same time, several companies outside the main indices have participated in the rally, helping total mcap reach a record even as major indices remain below their peaks," said Ankur Punj, MD, Equirus Wealth.The latest milestone has also coincided with a sharp recovery in equities. The Sensex and Nifty have gained more than 8.1% each in six consecutive sessions. The BSE MidCap 150 has advanced over 8.4% in eight of the past nine sessions, while the BSE SmallCap 250 has risen around 7% in seven of past eight sessions.Read more: Titan Q2 Results: Profit jumps 54% YoY to Rs 1,722 crore; total income up 25%The rally has been supported by a decline of more than 19% in crude oil prices over the past three sessions, easing concerns over inflation, India's import bill and the rupee. Strong foreign portfolio investor (FPI) buying, with net inflows of over $3.4 billion in the past 12 sessions, positive global cues, reduced uncertainty following the US midterm elections and better-than-expected second-quarter earnings have also lifted investor sentiment."The momentum could continue in the near term if crude prices remain stable at lower levels and foreign inflows sustain. However, investors should remain cautious as geopolitical developments, crude price volatility and profit booking after the sharp rally could limit further upside," said Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services.

articles.title: Demat account additions hit 9-month high in October as IPO boom draws investors
articles.summary: Mumbai: New demat account additions rose to a nine-month high in October, marking the fourth monthly increase in five months after a prolonged period of moderation between January 2025 and May 2026, as robust IPO activity drew more investors to the stock market.NSDL and CDSL together added nearly 3.36 million demat accounts in October, the highest monthly addition since January 2026. The total number of demat accounts stood at around 244 million at the end of the month. The number of demat accounts does not represent unique investors, as individuals can hold multiple accounts. The number of unique investors is estimated at around 136.6 million as of September, according to NSE data.Robust primary market activity was a key driver of the increase, with several large and smaller public issues attracting retail participation. October was the busiest month for IPO activity in 2026, with 13 issues raising a record ₹44,507 crore, including the Jio Platforms IPO - India's biggest ever.Read more: Why Nithin Kamath believes NRI investing in India has become easier than ever"Demat account openings typically rise when there is a surge in IPO activity, as investors open accounts to participate in public issues. The recent listing activity, including the large Jio Platform IPO and several smaller issues, has contributed to the increase," said Sunny Agrawal, head of fundamental equity research at SBICAPS Securities.Growing interest in gold and silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs) has also encouraged retail investors to open demat accounts, Agrawal said. Investors can purchase these products through the secondary market using a demat account.Read more: Equity mutual fund inflows may drop 18% in October as midcap and hybrid funds lose momentum: NomuraThe pickup in demat account additions came with gains in benchmark indices, with the Sensex rising 2% and the Nifty gaining 1.9% in October. However, broader market segments, which see greater retail participation, underperformed.

articles.title: Fed's Beth Hammack and Thomas Barkin favour gradual rate hikes as inflation stays high
articles.summary: Federal Reserve officials Beth Hammack and Thomas Barkin are making the case for a gradual approach to interest rate increases, signalling that policymakers remain focused on bringing inflation under control even as uncertainty over the economic outlook grows, Reuters reported.Their comments on Thursday come as the US central bank faces competing pressures from persistent price increases, geopolitical tensions and heavy investment in artificial intelligence (AI). The remarks also mark the first round of comments from Fed officials after Democrats won control of Congress and made gains in state level elections. For live updates on US Markets, click here "I expect that monetary policy will need to move to a restrictive stance to bring inflation back to 2% in a timely manner," Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said in a speech ahead of an event in Zurich.According to Reuters, Hammack, a consistent supporter of higher borrowing costs, favours smaller and more frequent adjustments rather than sharp increases. She said this approach would be less disruptive to households, businesses and financial markets. Gradual increases could also prevent an “inflationary mindset” from taking hold, she added.Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin echoed that view, saying inflation remained “too high” and was holding firm rather than easing. "When it comes to the pace of future rate hikes, gradual makes sense," he said.Inflation keeps pressure on the FedThe comments follow the Fed's decision last week to keep its benchmark interest rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range. Hammack, along with Fed Governor Lisa Cook, voted in favour of a rate increase, highlighting the divide among policymakers over how aggressively to tackle inflation.Also Read: Emerging markets lose $33.8 billion in October as investors flee Asian stocksFinancial markets broadly expect another increase in December, although expectations beyond that remain less certain. Reuters reported that futures traders have lowered the probability of a December hike to around 70% from more than 80% on Wednesday.AI investment and elections add to uncertaintyThe political shift could also influence the inflation outlook. Local voter opposition to data centres and permitting challenges could slow AI infrastructure spending, potentially easing demand for equipment and related resources.Evercore ISI analysts told clients on Wednesday that AI capital expenditure could slow in the next year or two, helping keep demand and supply in balance without requiring many more rate increases.TD Securities said it expects the Fed to raise rates by another 50 basis points by early next year. However, the brokerage said a resolution to the Iran war or a slowdown in AI investment could reduce the need for further tightening after March.Meanwhile, Friday's US jobs report is expected to provide another test for policymakers, with economists forecasting 65,000 additional jobs in October after September's 29,000 gain, Reuters reported.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.title: LTCG cut may come with a separate tax tweak
articles.summary: New Delhi/Mumbai: Key stakeholders are offering divergent prescriptions on how to address concerns over long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) tax and securities transaction tax (STT).These include scrapping LTCG altogether, removing it just for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), or lowering the rate. As for STT, suggestions include reducing it for some products and increasing it for others, people familiar with the discussions said."A well thought-out call would be taken," said an official. Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said she will consider investors' concerns regarding LTCG. These measures are being considered as a way of stemming the exodus of overseas investors that has led to a slump in Indian stock markets.While the LTCG collections amounted to ₹1.29 lakh crore in FY25, those for STT stood at ₹57,522 crore. Any call on the levies would have to take into account the revenue impact and funding for social sector schemes and subsidies.Finance ministry officials have met senior market participants to seek their views on capital market taxation. ET had reported on October 28 that the finance ministry officials had reached out to stakeholders on the issue.Financial sector regulators including the Reserve Bank of India and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) are understood to have backed the idea of doing away with LTCG to make India an attractive destination for foreign investors.Most participants favoured abolishing LTCG on equities while suggesting that the government could consider a marginal increase in STT on options trading alone, leaving cash and futures transactions untouched. They argued that options account for the bulk of daily trading activity and have been the focus of regulatory efforts to curb excessive speculation, people said.Some participants have cautioned against extending preferential tax treatment to FPIs alone, saying such a move could draw criticism from domestic investors. Short-term capital gains on listed equities, held for up to one year, are currently taxed at 20%, while long-term gains on holdings exceeding one year attract a 12.5% levy.Foreign portfolio investors have argued that several competing markets in the region do not levy LTCG, putting India at a disadvantage.Market participants said the combination of rupee depreciation and capital gains taxation has weighed on foreign investors' dollar-denominated post-tax returns, making other markets more attractive. One of the suggestions that has been put forth is calculating an FPI's taxable capital gains in dollar terms rather than rupees, said one of the persons.Separately, some FPI representatives also sought simplification of procedures governing the inflow and repatriation of foreign capital, calling for easier processes to bring funds into India and take money out of the country. Market participants said senior finance ministry officials have patiently heard out their suggestions.Another official said the implications of all suggestions would be examined before a final decision is reached.

articles.summary: Mumbai: Former Tata trustee Mehli Mistry has challenged his removal as a trustee of Bai Hirabai Jamsetji Bai Hirabai Charitable Institution (BHJTNCI), arguing that the decision was invalid and that some trustees who voted against his reappointment were themselves ineligible.In a series of rejoinders filed with the deputy charity commissioner for Greater Mumbai Region, Mistry has argued that the trust deed does not prescribe a fixed tenure for trustees or specify citizenship or tax residency as a qualification for trusteeship.He also accused Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) of attempting to prevent scrutiny of alleged governance lapses, including commissions and financial benefits received by trustees. The matter has been adjourned to December 3. Challenging the recording of his cessation as a BHJTNCI trustee with effect from October 28, 2025, Mistry argued that neither the trust's 1913 will nor its 1923 trust deed prescribes a fixed tenure for trustees.The trust's position that his three-year term had expired relied on a 2022 circular and appointment letter, but neither of them can override the governing instruments, he argued.Citing Clause 23 of the deed, Mistry said vacancies arise on grounds including death, permanent residence outside the Bombay Presidency, insolvency, renunciation of faith and unfitness, but not on expiry of a fixed term. The codicil also says trustees "shall always be trustees," he added.Mistry argued that he is not a "tenure trustee" under Section 2(17A) introduced through an 2025 amendment and that Section 30A(1), therefore, does not apply to him. He also cited the trust's annexures, which allegedly show different renewal periods for other trustees, including about two years for Vijay Singh and less than two years for Venu Srinivasan."The trust cannot use Section 30A(1) as a sword to oust the objector on October 28, 2025, and, in the same breath, ignore that very provision when its own vice chairman (Singh) acted in breach of it on that very day. A party cannot approbate and reprobate," Mistry said in his submission.He also cited a resolution passed on October 17, 2024, at a joint meeting of SDTT and Sir Ratan Tata Trust trustees, shortly after Ratan Tata's death. The resolution provided for trustees to be reappointed on expiry of their terms without any limit on tenure, he said.The trust deliberately omitted it from its reply to his complaint, Mistry claimed.He urged the authority to reject BHJTNCI's change report against him as "illegal, non-est and contrary to the trust deed."According to Mistry, Circular Resolution No 671 of October 23, 2025, proposing his reappointment, was approved by Jehangir H C Jehangir and Darius Khambata but was not approved by Noel Tata, Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh. Jimmy Tata did not respond.He said the trust failed to follow the 2024 resolution's requirement of unanimous approval.In a 24-page rejoinder filed under Section 22 of the Maharashtra Public Trusts Act, 1950, Mistry also contested the trust's objections to his citizenship and tax residency, saying the will, codicil or trust deed does not prescribe these as criteria for trusteeship."If foreign citizenship and overseas residence are to be treated as relevant considerations, they must be examined in relation to the reporting trustee with equal rigour," he further said and alleged that Noel Tata, the current reporting trustee, is an Irish citizen, a UAE tax resident and a UAE Golden Visa holder.He sought an affidavit from Tata detailing his citizenship and tax residency history, including whether he has held a Swiss passport.
