articles.summary: BSE on Wednesday reported a 44.9% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 809.15 crore for the second quarter of FY27 (Q2FY27), compared with Rs 558.43 crore in the corresponding period last year (Q2FY26).The exchange's revenue for the quarter increased 34.1% to Rs 1,432.6 crore from Rs 1,068.4 crore a year ago.Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 42.4% year-on-year to Rs 984 crore, compared with Rs 690.9 crore in the year-ago quarter.EBITDA margin expanded to 68.7% from 64.66% in the corresponding quarter last year.Transaction charges rose 42% year-on-year to Rs 1,127.8 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 794 crore in Q2FY26.Treasury income on clearing and settlement funds declined 14% to Rs 36.5 crore from Rs 42.8 crore reported in the year-ago period.BSE's total operating expenses increased 21% year-on-year to Rs 494.7 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 410.1 crore in Q2FY26.On a standalone basis, BSE's net profit after tax rose 50.3% year-on-year to Rs 773.4 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 514.5 crore in the corresponding quarter of FY26. Revenue from operations increased 38.3% to Rs 1,349.3 crore from Rs 975.5 crore in Q2FY26.Board approves appointment of Ashutosh Singh as executive directorThe board of directors has approved the appointment of Ashutosh Singh (DIN: 10579541) as Executive Director – Business (Vertical 3) for a period of five years, effective November 30, 2026, subject to ratification of his appointment by the shareholders. The appointment follows the company's earlier intimations dated June 2, 2026, and October 21, 2026.The board has also approved a proposal to accept an offer from the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) for the allotment of a plot at Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC), Mumbai. The proposed plot will be used to develop additional premises and infrastructure facilities for the company. The transaction is subject to completion of the necessary documentation, fulfilment of applicable conditions and execution of definitive agreements with MMRDA.BSE's top shareholdersAs of September 2026, the Life Insurance Corporation of India was BSE's largest shareholder, with a 4.44% stake, followed by ICICI Prudential Focus Equity Fund at 2.70% and SBI Nifty 50 ETF at 2.57%.Nippon Life India Trustee Ltd – A/c Nippon India Growth Fund held a 1.84% stake, while Siddharth Balachandran owned 1.64%. Kotak Flexicap Fund held 1.52%, followed by Tata AIA Life Insurance Co Ltd – Whole Life Mid Cap at 1.42%. Invesco India Mid Cap Fund held a 1.25% stake, UTI Nifty 50 ETF owned 1.22%, while S Gopalakrishnan held 1.17%.BSE share priceAhead of its Q2 results announcement, BSE shares settled 1.75% lower at Rs 3,601.50 on the NSE, against the previous closing price. The stock has a 52-week trading range of Rs 2,377 to Rs 4,447, while its year-to-date return stood at 37%.BSE had a market capitalisation of Rs 1,46,899 crore on the NSE, as of November 4.

articles.title: US: What happens next as Dems take over
articles.summary: Washington: Democrats are preparing a legislative offensive against US President Donald Trump after their sweeping midterm victory handed them control of both chambers of Congress and the power to challenge his policies, investigate his administration and block his nominees.Emboldened by victories deep in traditional Republican territory, the party is promising swift action on living costs and the war in Iran, while signaling that investigations of alleged abuses and corruption will be a major priority.Also read | Did Iran war just blow up in Trump's face?House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is in line to become the first Black speaker when the new Congress takes office in January, vowed to go after what he described as "unprecedented corruption" in the government."Because if you have people in high office who are so focused on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends, or their donors, then they're not focused on making life better for the American people," he said.But Democrats will not have a free hand. Trump retains his veto, while Senate rules allow Republicans to obstruct most legislation.Here are the opportunities -- and obstacles -- ahead.First 100 hoursJeffries has promised an ambitious legislative push in the House's first 100 hours, focused on affordability -- the issue that dominated an election shaped by tariffs, high prices and the Iran war.His priorities include restoring expired Affordable Care Act health insurance subsidies, reversing nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts enacted under Trump, rolling back tariffs and pressing for an end to the conflict, which has sent fuel costs soaring.With majorities in both chambers, Democrats can bring their proposals to votes and take charge of spending negotiations. They could use federal budget deadlines to demand concessions, although confrontations over spending risk government shutdowns.'Lawyer up'Oversight may offer an even more immediate means of challenging Trump.Robert Garcia, the Democrat expected to chair the powerful House Oversight Committee, fired off a blunt election-night message to Republicans on social media: "LAWYER UP."Also read | What Trump & Republicans' loss means for IndiaOregon Senator Ron Wyden was even more concise, posting a single word: "Subpoenas."With control of committees in both chambers, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, potentially putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny.Likely subjects include the Trump family's business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war.Democrats have also signaled interest in the handling of files relating to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.The administration could resist demands for testimony or documents, triggering court battles.Democrats could pursue Trump's third impeachment, though party leaders have not committed to doing so. The House needs only a simple majority to impeach, but removing a president requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate -- far beyond the party's numbers.Senate muscleThe Senate majority gives Democrats another powerful lever: control of confirmations.They can block Trump's judicial and cabinet nominees, including any selection to fill a Supreme Court vacancy, potentially curbing his influence over the courts long after he leaves office.Also read | Vivek Ramaswamy: Decoding a Republican firebrand's high-decibel fallDemocratic Senate chairs will also decide which bills and investigations receive committee attention.Limits and dealsPassing laws will be much harder than launching investigations.Most legislation must clear a 60-vote hurdle in the Senate to overcome procedural obstruction. Trump can veto bills passed by Congress, and overturning a veto requires two-thirds support in both chambers.He also retains substantial executive powers over immigration, trade and military operations, although lawmakers can seek to constrain them through legislation and spending decisions.Trump struck a conciliatory note after the rout, praising Democrats for doing a "good job" and telling The New York Times that he would accept the result and expected to work with them.He even raised the possibility of cooperation on immigration.But he had previously warned that if Democrats won Congress, "I veto everything" -- a reminder that the next two years could be defined as much by confrontation as compromise.

articles.title: IMA welcomes rank-based system in Neet, seeks safeguards to protect merit

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has given in-principle approval to replacing the existing percentile-based system with a rank-based merit system for admissions to postgraduate and super-speciality medical courses. Under the proposed arrangement, only ranks, and not percentile scores, will be declared in examination results.
The proposed system is yet to be notified through final NMC regulations. A draft regulation is expected to be issued for stakeholder consultation.

articles.title: Cabinet clears ₹14,500 cr funding scheme for battery energy storage systems
articles.summary:
The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved Rs 14,500 crore in viability gap funding for 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage systems between FY27 and FY31.
This development is significant given India's ambitious target of 500 GW of renewable energy by 2030.
The scheme is aimed at supporting the development of 92 GWh storage capacity across three technologies -- Battery Energy Storage System (30 GWh), Pumped Storage Projects (60 GWh) and Emerging Storage Technologies (2GW), Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said in a media briefing here.
The minister said the scheme will be implemented for five years till 2030-31.

The proposal has been submitted under the direction of Commerce and Transport Minister Bibhuti Bhushan Jena as part of the state's efforts to strengthen EV infrastructure, they said.
In the first phase of the scheme, the Centre has approved the setting up of 170 EV charging stations in seven major cities, and work on the project is currently underway, an official statement said.

articles.title: Govt approves strengthening of fast track courts to deal with child abuse
articles.summary:
The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved the strengthening and extension of 850 fast track courts to deal with child abuse and rape cases, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said.
Briefing reporters on decisions taken by the Cabinet, Vaishnaw said the Modi government is committed to firmly dealing with cases of atrocities against women and children.
He said the decision is part of efforts to fully utilise and implement prevailing laws and draft new legislations to deal with such cases.
The Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the establishment of Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), including exclusive POCSO (ePOCSO) courts, was introduced in October 2019, following the enactment of the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 and the order of the Supreme Court.
These courts are dedicated to the time-bound trial and disposal of pending cases related to rape and crimes under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012.

Falling Stocks, Surging Stocks, High Valuations: Sanjoy Bhattacharyya on Navigating a Tough Market
articles.summary: After a decade of largely positive returns, Indian markets could be heading towards their first negative year. The market has been virtually flat for more than years, valuations remain demanding and sharp sector rotations have made investing increasingly challenging. In this Diwali special of the Moneycontrol Wealth Formula podcast, market veteran Sanjoy Bhattacharyya of Fortuna Capital joins Mahalakshmi for a deep-dive into how investors should navigate this phase. With over three decades of experience, Sanjoy shares his investment philosophy and explains why surviving difficult markets matters more than chasing spectacular returns. In this conversation: Why high valuations and a flood of IPOs have weighed on market returns Why investing is 85–90% temperament and only 10–15% intellect How to identify businesses that can deliver sustainable growth without excessive capital The biggest warning signs: weak management, poor governance, debt and related-party transactions When a sharp fall in a stock is an opportunity — and when it is a warning Why investors must reassess their losers and learn to cut their losses The dangers of FOMO, overconfidence and trying to get rich quickly Why the best way to build wealth is to think like a businessman and own enduring businesses Sanjay also discusses investment lessons from companies such as IEX, Kingfa, Laurus Labs and Infosys. The big takeaway: Don't chase the market. Protect your capital, stay patient and focus on owning good businesses. A special Diwali conversation on investing, temperament and the art of surviving market cycles.

articles.title: Will Republicans learn from this defeat?
articles.summary: A healthy Republican Party would respond to this historic midterm-election repudiation of President Donald Trump with contrition and honest introspection. Its leaders would plot a fresh path forward and shed the elements of a White House agenda that drove American voters to hand control of the House of Representatives and US Senate to a Democratic Party they don’t even approve of all that much.Reduced to a rump in Congress and its governing coalition gutted to the bone — just in time for 2028 — that Republican Party would assemble a more durable confederation of voters that doesn’t rise and fall on the whims of a narcissistic albeit once-in-a-generation political talent.But Republicans and their exalted leader aren’t the picture of political health.Those within the party most likely to confront reality and take on the difficult work of rebuilding the GOP were cut down in ruby-red House districts, Senate seats and governors’ mansions that have simply not elected Democrats. The only Republicans left standing were insulated — by gerrymandered districts, their constituents’ stubborn support for Trump or a combination of the two. The party’s short-sighted motivation will be to follow the president’s defiant lead and resist the new Democratic majorities’ attempts to neuter the commander-in-chief.And so the party’s future, immediate and otherwise, is in Trump’s hands, and most elected officials would still take their cues from the White House.As the shocking returns flowed in showing defeats in Senate contests in Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas (Texas!), some veteran party insiders I spoke with disagreed with my assessment and argued that battered congressional Republicans would be chastened, distance themselves from Trump and finally end blind support for his agenda on Capitol Hill. Some Republican operatives even speculated that Vice President JD Vance would be forced to abandon any plans he might have to seek the White House, to say nothing of aspiring Cabinet members.I’m not a gambler. But if I were, I wouldn’t risk a nickel on that bet. The siren song of the president’s loyal, Make American Great Again (MAGA) populist base will be hard for the party’s 2028 contenders to resist — and that’s if a major effort materializes to wean the party off of Trump.This isn’t the first time the president has led his party into a ditch, only to recover like Lazarus because he refused to concede failure. That kind of obstinance inspires grassroots conservatives who see a fighter rather than a shirker. “I wasn’t on the ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” Trump said in a Truth Social post on election night. Meanwhile, GOP strategists told me with a high degree of confidence that Democrats will overplay their hand — just like Republicans did — causing voters to turn back to Trump and the GOP just in time for a presidential campaign now unexpectedly ripe with opportunity.The claim that Democrats will overreach and offer Republicans a chance to revive their political standing is not unreasonable; the US has seen both political parties misinterpret an election backlash. The Democrats did so following back-to-back blue waves in 2006 and 2008. Two years later in 2010, a red wave gained the GOP 63 House districts and seven Senate seats during President Barack Obama’s first midterm election. The Republicans committed the same faux pas during Trump’s first presidency, which fueled a blue wave-flip of 41 House districts in the 2018 midterm election.No doubt, if Democrats dive head first into impeaching Trump and legislate on culture-war issues after the new Congress is seated in January, voters will sour on them rather quickly. But I wonder if Republicans have digested the breadth of the destruction the 45th and 47th president left in his wake this week — an apocalyptic political disaster that, as polling analyst Sean Trende points out, hasn’t been seen since 1974, in the aftermath of the Watergate scandal that left the GOP on life support.Republicans didn’t just lose a Senate seat in Kansas for the first time in nearly a century. The Democrats were possibly poised to win a Senate seat in Mississippi for the first time since 1982. The GOP lost states, districts and other offices that Trump and his GOP predecessors have been carrying by double digits going back years, if not decades. That outcome demands a wholesale reevaluation of American politics and the blue-state, red-state paradigm the US has lived under for a quarter century.Trump doesn’t seem much interested in doing so. And if past is prologue, that means Republicans won’t be either. They might need to lose some more, first.

articles.title: Trump accepts defeat, hints at future role as ‘pundit’
Decoding a Rep firebrand's high-decibel fall
articles.summary: Vivek Ramaswamy's meteoric rise was built on the promise that an outsider equipped with sharp rhetoric, business credentials and unwavering loyalty to Donald Trump could reshape the fortunes of the Republican Party. His defeat in Ohio at the US midterms today could be proof that national-level visibility, proximity to the president and political acumen may not be enough to convert big political fame into a poll success story.Democrat Amy Acton defeated the Trump-backed Ramaswamy in the Ohio governor's race, ending Republican control of the state governor office and delivering Democrats their first victory in the contest in 20 years.Also read | US has no immediate plan to strike Iran, Trump tells FTJust ahead of the vote, Ramaswamy drew public attention in stunning fashion by bringing out a highly controversial ad based on an episode from Acton's personal life. The ad eventually went on to divide opinions like few other ads in recent memory.As Ramaswamy's camapaign for the high-profile seat got progressively heated up, Trump and Vice-President JD Vance repeatedly travelled to Ohio to campaign for him.The win for Acton, who also became the first woman elected governor of Ohio, came despite more than $100 million being spent against her on the strength of substantial financial backing from Ramaswamy's allies.Decoding a high-profile lossRamaswamy's defeat is significant because he was more than an ordinary Republican gubernatorial candidate. The biotech entrepreneur had emerged as one of the most recognisable faces of the party's new generation, using television debates, social media and provocative political arguments to build a national following.His 2021 bestseller Woke, Inc. helped establish his credentials as an anti-woke conservative. During the 2024 Republican presidential primaries, his combative debate performances and uncompromising positions attracted considerable attention, even though he eventually finished fourth in the Iowa caucuses before withdrawing and endorsing Trump.Also read | 'We would have won a landslide': Trump claims Republicans would have won big if on ballotHis political ascent also earned him a brief role alongside Elon Musk in the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE).His ability to articulate the MAGA movement's positions with unusual energy made him an influential political communicator. He also helped broaden the Republican Party's appeal by demonstrating that its conservative nationalist message could be championed by an Indian-American Hindu.His defeat is now raising questions about whether national fame can translate into support at the state level.The limits of MAGAFor Trump, the result could be a marked setback. Ramaswamy had the president's backing, substantial campaign resources and support from prominent Republicans. These big advantages, however, failed to overcome voter concerns about affordability, rising living costs and fuel prices.Acton, on the other hands, made these issues central to her campaign, which likely played a huge role in giving her the win.Ramaswamy's loss also might go on to show that Trump's political influence has limits, particularly when voters are focused on other important issues.The ad featuring Acton's estranged mother may have added a major layer of complication to Ramaswamy's campaign. The advertisement divided opinions sharply and drew fierce criticism from both Republicans and Democrats.Trump publicly defended Ramaswamy's ad and his decision to run it. It probably turned out to be one of the factors that backfired on their high-decibel campaign, with voters taking strong issue with a move made in bad taste.No country for loud menFor Republicans, Ohio may have just offered a warning -- that political savvy, money & fundraising muscle and sleek rhetoric don't guarantee a win.For Ramaswamy, this defeat does not diminish him or erode his ability to shape conservative debates. What it actually does is, it exposes the gap between being a MAGA bigshot and turning that into a poll win.Some analysts also said this loss might also toughen things for new Republican faces hoping to inherit Trump's legacy. Ramaswamy had positioned himself as a flagbearer of that generation. His fall may have just suggested that the party's future will depend not just on sharp rhetoric and money power, but also on how it addresses actual socio-economic issues.

articles.title: DDCA seeks venue change for India-Sri Lanka ODI over pollution concerns
articles.summary:
The opening One-Day International between India and Sri Lanka slated to be played in the national capital on December 13 is likely to be moved out due to pollution and outfield revamp.
With pollution at its peak in the months of November and December being a major factor, the Delhi and District Cricket Association has requested the BCCI to move the game out of Delhi also because of the outfield work currently underway at the Feroz Shah Kotla.
A sand-based outfield is being laid and the work will go on for the next three months.
"Pollution is a major factor and then there is renovation work going on. So we have requested the BCCI to move the game out of Delhi," a DDCA source told PTI.
India and Sri Lanka are scheduled to play three ODIs and as many T20Is in December.

articles.title: Explained: Why Sebi wants mutual fund investors to switch to direct plans
articles.summary: Sebi has directed mutual fund houses to make direct plans the default option on their digital platforms from 1st November. A look at the reason behind the regulator’s action.WHAT ARE DIRECT AND REGULAR PLANS IN MUTUAL FUNDS?Direct and regular plans are two ways of investing in a mutual fund scheme. In a direct plan, investors put money in a scheme without involving a distributor, broker or agent. Since no commission is paid, the scheme’s expense ratio or fee is lower.A regular plan is bought through a distributor, broker or adviser. The mutual fund pays a commission to the intermediary, and this cost is recovered from the investor through the scheme’s expense ratio. As a result, the expense ratio is higher than that of direct plans.According to the latest AMFI data, the total expense ratio (TER) of regular plans ranges from 0.36% to 4.3%, compared with 0% to 2.7% for direct plans.WHAT HAS SEBI CHANGED AND WHY?From November 1, Sebi has asked mutual fund houses to make direct plans the default option on their websites and mobile apps. So, if an investor visits a fund house’s app to invest in an equity scheme, the direct plan will now be pre-selected or displayed as the primary option. Investors can still choose regular plans if they want distributor assistance.Read more: Sebi levies Rs 40 lakh penalty on four entities in Axis MF front-running caseBUT WHAT’S WRONG WITH REGULAR PLANS?There is nothing wrong per se with regular plans. In fact, it may be suitable for investors seeking professional guidance or those new to mutual funds. After all, distributors handle the client portfolios and do periodic reviews of the holdings.But, critics point out that in addition to the higher costs, regular plans could result in conflict of interest. Since distributors are paid commissions by fund houses, this would push some intermediaries to recommend schemes that offer higher commissions rather than those best suited for client needs. They claim investors would be better off availing the services of fee-based financial advisers, who charge investors directly for their advice.HOW MUCH MONEY CAN INVESTORS SAVE THROUGH LOWER EXPENSE RATIOS?While the difference in the total expense ratio may appear small, it can significantly impact returns over long investment horizons.For instance, an investor putting Rs 20,000 a month into an equity mutual fund for 15 years, assuming annual returns of 12%, could accumulate around Rs 94.4 lakh in a direct plan with a 0.7% expense ratio. In comparison, the corpus would be about Rs 86 lakh in a regular plan with a 1.7% expense ratio.The difference arises because lower expenses leave more money invested, allowing returns to compound over time.Read more: Quant Mutual Fund reduces exposure to frontline IT stocks as part of profit-booking exerciseWHO SHOULD CONSIDER DIRECT PLANS?Direct plans are suitable for investors who can research funds, monitor their portfolios and make investment decisions independently or with the help of fee-based advisors.If you understand concepts such as asset allocation, risk management and portfolio rebalancing, and can stay invested through market cycles, a direct plan may be a good option.

'Tesla misled South Korean customers'
articles.summary: Tesla has misled tens of thousands of South Korean customers by marketing driver-assistance software that the company knows cannot be legally used in most of its vehicles in the country, according to a complaint an advocacy group plans to file with a consumer protection agency on Thursday.Tesla has marketed Full Self-Driving (Supervised) software to prospective buyers in South Korea for years, often collecting lump-sum payments of 9.043 million won ($6,726).FSD can be used on about 20% of Tesla vehicles registered in South Korea - those manufactured in the US, Tesla Korea country manager Seo Young-deuk said in parliamentary testimony last month. Those cars meet US vehicle-safety standards that South Korea recognizes as part of a free trade agreement, according to the forthcoming complaint to the Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC), seen by Reuters.The complaint to the regulator, which also handles antitrust, has not been previously reported.Most Tesla vehicles in South Korea, however, are manufactured in China, where no such agreement exists. Tesla only recently started the process for obtaining FSD certification for China-made vehicles, despite charging customers for the software for more than three years.SOUTH KOREAN TRADE COMMISSION INVESTIGATINGIt is unclear how many South Korean customers purchased FSD subscriptions on ineligible vehicles, but Tesla has sold more than 170,000 Shanghai-produced vehicles in South Korea since 2023, according to Tesla data sent to South Korea's National Assembly."Tesla generated substantial revenue by selling an expensive driver-assistance system to mass-market buyers who cannot use it for even a single day," said Choi Young-suk, who leads automotive issues at the advocacy group Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty.Tesla did not respond to requests for comment. A KFTC official said the agency launched a probe earlier this year into Tesla's advertising of its FSD system and has received written responses from the company, but declined to provide further details.Tesla continued to market FSD as sales of ineligible China-manufactured Teslas surged in South Korea in recent years. Sales of FSD-incompatible Teslas made in China grew more than fivefold in South Korea from 2023 through last year, when 99% of new Teslas sold in South Korea could not legally use FSD, according to data Tesla submitted to the National Assembly.Despite years of promises from CEO Elon Musk that all Teslas would soon become fully driverless vehicles, FSD is not autonomous and requires active human supervision.Tesla has sought to expand FSD's reach beyond North America, particularly in Europe, where the company has waged a pressure campaign against European regulators.TESLA SALES SURGE IN SOUTH KOREATesla surpassed BMW this year as South Korea's top imported-car brand, according to South Korean import data.Tesla sold FSD for one-time payments for years, before shifting to a monthly subscription of 150,000 won ($112) in August.The complaint alleges that Tesla promoted FSD last year as "coming soon" and posted a demonstration video filmed in South Korea without clearly disclosing that the technology could only be used in a small fraction of Teslas being sold.Tesla knew those limitations but continued to market the software to all customers, the complaint said.Tesla Korea manager Seo testified during an October 8 parliamentary hearing that the company had not formally requested FSD testing from the transport ministry. Two weeks later, Tesla applied for certification.The ministry said FSD does not comply with local safety rules, including requirements for drivers to keep their hands on the wheel, according to a statement it sent to a lawmaker, reviewed by Reuters. The transport ministry could not be reached for comment.The consumer group accused Tesla Korea of deceptive marketing and asked the KFTC to issue a temporary cease-and-desist order on marketing FSD for ineligible vehicles, impose administrative fines and refer the case to state investigators.

articles.title: China curbs cloud SK Hynix’s NY chip plans
articles.summary: US officials have held up approval for American chipmaking equipment needed by SK Hynix to expand production in China, complicating the South Korean chipmaker's plans for new memory-chip plants in New York, according to people familiar with the matter.SK Hynix is seeking US export licenses to equip its Dalian plant, arguing that increased production there would help fund its planned US expansion. But the Commerce Department has yet to approve the new licenses, the people said.Its Solidigm unit plans to invest about $45 billion and build two NAND plants in Marcy, New York, two people said, with investment potentially reaching about $100 billion over time. NAND is memory that retains data even when power is turned off and is used for storage in data centers.Also Read | Samsung to make AMD, Nvidia chip parts at second Texas plant: ReportTRUMP ADMINISTRATION FACES POLICY DILEMMAThe negotiations raise questions about how far the Trump administration is willing to bend national security guardrails established to keep US technology from aiding China's military, in order to bring foreign investment and chipmaking onshore."Ultimately, none of this is going to go forward without a green light from the White House," said Leland Miller, a member of the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, a bipartisan panel created by the US Congress. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Negotiations are continuing, the people said, with approval for the Dalian expansion central to SK Hynix's plans in New York.Also Read | Japan to invest up to $21 billion in two US chip factories to be run by GlobalFoundriesCOMMERCE DEPARTMENT MEETINGS INTENSIFYExecutives from SK Hynix's US subsidiary, Solidigm, have met nearly 10 times with officials from the Commerce Department since late August, one of the people said. The company needs to ramp up production and develop more sophisticated NAND chipmaking in China to generate revenue to build a US facility and to stay competitive, the people said.In a meeting last week, Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler held to his position that the US would not allow more American chipmaking tools to upgrade or expand capacity, the person said, though the department has not formally denied a license to export American equipment to fill empty clean space in Dalian. The two sides are also negotiating a separate license for 2027 for equipment to keep up the Dalian facility, the person said.A spokesperson for the Department of Commerce did not immediately respond to a request for comment.In a statement last week, Solidigm said: "As a US-founded and headquartered company, Solidigm regularly evaluates strategic alternatives to best serve its customers and enhance its long-term competitiveness. The company is currently exploring options for building a NAND memory fab at potential locations around the world. No decision regarding any specific course of action has been made." Solidigm stuck to its statement from last week. SK Hynix did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside business hours.

articles.title: IDBI Bank Strike: What's on November 10?
articles.summary: A two-day nationwide strike by IDBI Bank officers and employees against the proposed sale of a majority stake in the lender to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings ended on Tuesday. The employees' union will decide its next course of action at a meeting on November 10 as it continues to oppose the disinvestment. The strike was called by the United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees, which is seeking to stop the proposed transaction. The union said the protest received a strong response from employees and officers across the country."The strike got a massive response from employees and officers across the country. We will decide the future course of action in our core committee meeting post Diwali on November 10 on the way to intensify struggle," United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees convener Devidas Tuljapurkar said.Read more - Get ready to pay double for parking in Delhi: MCD plans to hike charges at 400 parking lots under GRAP-II; what two-wheeler and car owners need to knowHe added that the union would approach the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) to seek wider support, including the possibility of a nationwide bank strike.IDBI Bank employees oppose proposed stake sale to FairfaxThe union has raised concerns about the valuation of the lender and the possibility of its assets and business capabilities being undervalued in the transaction."We are seriously concerned that the transaction may undervalue IDBI’s properties, institutional capabilities, customer relationships, future earnings and strategic importance," Tuljapurkar said.Read more - Rahul Gandhi vs Narendra Modi debate: RaGa asks public if they want open face-off; urges Nitin Gadkari, Yogi Adityanath & other BJP leaders to convince PMHe also called on the government to make the valuation process more transparent. The union wants the government to disclose the valuation methodology, the assumptions used, how real estate and other assets have been assessed, and the reasons for accepting the proposed sale price.Tuljapurkar said the public should have clear evidence that a national asset was not being transferred at a throwaway price. He also called for scrutiny of the proposed buyer's ownership structure, financial position, regulatory record and any substantiated controversies in its home jurisdiction.Congress calls IDBI Bank disinvestment a 'scam'The proposed sale has also drawn criticism from the Opposition. The Congress on Monday described the IDBI Bank disinvestment as a 'scam' and demanded that the government stop the sale to a foreign company and set up a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) to investigate the process.Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh alleged that a foreign company was acquiring the lender using funds belonging to the bank itself."This is yet another major scam by the Modi government, which warrants an investigation. We demand that the process of selling IDBI Bank to a foreign company be halted," Ramesh said in a post on X.IDBI Bank stake sale: Government, LIC to sell 60.72% stakeThe Central government on October 14 approved the sale of a combined 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings for around Rs 53,000 crore (USD 5.5 billion).Under the proposed transaction, Fairfax will acquire the government's 30.48% stake, valued at around Rs 26,620 crore, and LIC's 30.24% holding, worth approximately Rs 26,440 crore.The Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa-led Fairfax will pay Rs 81 per share, above the benchmark fair value of Rs 75.99 determined by two independent valuation agencies.The deal, if completed, would mark one of the largest foreign investments in an Indian bank and a major step in the country's long-delayed banking privatisation programme.The Central government currently holds 45.48% of IDBI Bank, while LIC owns 49.24%. The transaction is expected to be completed by the end of the current financial year, subject to regulatory clearance from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).How many employees does IDBI Bank have?IDBI Bank has 19,108 employees on its rolls, including 9,500 employees from Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Other Backward Classes categories.The lender also has 6,911 women employees and 884 employees with disabilities. The proposed stake sale has therefore become a major concern for the employees' union, which is seeking clarity on the transaction and its implications.Inputs from PTI

articles.title: US job openings increase by 333,000 in Sept
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, - US job openings increased sharply in September while layoffs fell, supporting economists' views that the labor market remained on firmer footing despite tepid employment gains during that month.Job openings, a measure of labor demand, had risen by 333,000 to 7.523 million by the last day of September, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said in its Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, or JOLTS report, on Tuesday. Data for August was revised slightly higher to show 7.190 million vacancies instead of the previously reported 7.079 million.Click here to track US midterm election results 2026 live updates Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 7.100 million unfilled positions in September. The job openings rate rose to 4.5% from 4.3% in August. The JOLTS report has been plagued by a low response rate, which has decreased considerably from the period prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.Economists view the labor market as continuing to be in a "low-hire, low-fire" state, and argue that strong profits as domestic demand remains resilient were keeping layoffs near historic lows. The ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran is, however, making employers hesitant to boost hiring, they said.Hiring increased by 131,000 to 5.402 million in September. The hires rate rose to 3.4% from 3.3% in August. Layoffs and discharges decreased by 127,000 to 1.641 million, with the rate falling to 1.0% from 1.1% in August.Nonfarm payrolls increased by 29,000 jobs in September. A Reuters survey of economists expects payrolls to have advanced by 65,000 in October. The unemployment rate is forecast to have been unchanged at 4.2%.

articles.title: Deficient monsoon slows rabi sowing, wheat sowing yet to pick up pace
articles.summary:
Sowing of rabi crops, including wheat, has fallen sharply behind last year's pace, with the area covered down 46 per cent at 37.56 lakh hectare as of October 30, compared to 69.02 lakh hectare in the same period a year ago, according to data released by the Union Agriculture Ministry.
Wheat, the principal rabi crop, was sown over just 19,000 hectare, against 3.34 lakh hectare last year, a shortfall attributed to insufficient soil moisture.
The crop is usually sown in October-November and harvested in March-April.
In the 2025-26 crop year (July-June), wheat was planted on 336 lakh hectare.
According to the weekly data, area under pulses stood at 9.45 lakh hectare, down from 19.56 lakh hectare. Gram acreage fell to 5.90 lakh hectare from 14.35 lakh hectare.
Oilseeds were sown over 20.97 lakh hectare, compared to 38.62 lakh hectare a year ago. Within this, rapeseed and mustard covered 20.50 lakh hectare, against 38.07 lakh hectare.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu live tracker
articles.summary: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu crossed the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, early on Tuesday, November 3, with wind speeds of 100-110 kmph and gusts reaching 120 kmph, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. The landfall took place between 3:30 am and 5:30 am IST, with the storm's centre located near latitude 15.53°N and longitude 80.22°E.The landfall process began around 1 am and continued for several hours, with the storm's spiral bands and wall cloud moving over the coastline before its eye reached land. Heavy rainfall associated with Murasu has affected several parts of Vijayawada, leaving roads waterlogged and disrupting traffic.Tamil Nadu has sent 500 electricity department personnel in 25 teams to help Andhra Pradesh restore power supply, while three NDRF teams comprising 90 personnel have also been deployed for rescue and relief operations.— Indiametdept (@Indiametdept) Cyclone Murasu live updates: Latest developments6:40 am: Cyclone Murasu crosses Andhra Pradesh coast near OngoleThe IMD said Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu moved north-northwestwards and crossed the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, between 3:30 am and 5:30 am IST on Tuesday. The storm crossed near latitude 15.53°N and longitude 80.22°E, with sustained wind speeds of 100-110 kmph and gusts reaching 120 kmph.4:30 am: Cyclone's eye touches Andhra Pradesh coastThe landfall process continued, with part of the storm's wall cloud entering land in its forward sector. The IMD said the eye of Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu was touching the south Andhra Pradesh coast.3:30 am: Inner spiral band and wall cloud move over coastThe IMD reported that the landfall process was continuing, with the inner spiral band in the northern sector entering south coastal Andhra Pradesh. The storm's wall cloud region was also moving over land.2:30 am: Landfall process begins along south Andhra Pradesh coastThe IMD said the landfall process of Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu began around 1 am on Tuesday over south coastal Andhra Pradesh.Heavy rain leaves roads waterlogged in VijayawadaHeavy rainfall under the influence of Murasu has affected several parts of Vijayawada. The downpour began late Monday night and continued into the early hours of Tuesday, leaving roads waterlogged and disrupting movement.Several major roads, including Bandar Road and Polyclinic Road, reported waterlogging. Parts of One Town were also affected, causing inconvenience to commuters.Tamil Nadu sends 500 electricity personnel to Andhra PradeshTamil Nadu has deployed 500 electricity department personnel in 25 teams to help Andhra Pradesh restore power supply disrupted by the cyclone.Tamil Nadu Electricity Minister R Nirmal Kumar said the deployment followed a request from Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu. The teams will assist with electricity restoration work in the neighbouring state.Three NDRF teams deployed for rescue and relief operationsThree National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams, comprising 90 personnel, have been deployed from the force's 4th Battalion near Arakkonam in Tamil Nadu to support disaster management efforts in Andhra Pradesh.Each team consists of 30 personnel, with deployments planned for areas including Nellore, Prakasam and Markapuram. The teams will assist with rescue operations, debris clearance and relief work in affected areas.Odisha on alert as IMD forecasts heavy rainfallThe southern districts of Odisha were also placed under a heavy rainfall warning as Murasu affected weather conditions along the east coast. The IMD forecast rainfall of 7 cm to 20 cm on November 2 and 3. Parts of the state were also likely to experience winds of 50-60 kmph, with gusts reaching 70 kmph, on November 3.The NDRF and Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) were kept on standby in vulnerable areas. Fishermen were advised not to venture into the sea between November 2 and 4.In Ganjam district, officials were directed to stock essential supplies and move residents from high-risk areas to designated shelters as part of cyclone preparedness measures.

articles.title: US Supreme Court rejects Trump admin's push to set aside California ballots
articles.summary:
The Supreme Court on Monday rejected a push for California to set aside thousands of mail ballots from people President Donald Trump's administration claims are noncitizens, a decision that comes on the eve of the pivotal midterm elections.
The high court refused to intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state's voter rolls.
It was the latest in a flurry of election-related litigation the day before the midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress for the last two years of Trump's second term.
In California, the Trump administration had asked the high court to set aside the challenged ballots until the voters' citizenship status could be verified. But officials there said that the list appeared to be filled with errors and that setting the ballots aside could effectively disenfranchise legal voters.
The high court did not detail its reasoning, as is common in emergency decisions.

articles.title: US consortium pushes for $4.4 billion LNG project in Pakistan: Report
articles.summary:
A consortium of American companies, backed by US President Donald Trump's administration, is seeking up to USD 4.4 billion in investment for an integrated liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Pakistan, according to a media report on Monday.
The proposed project will cover imports, storage, regasification, gas transmission and sales to large consumers on a merchant basis, the Dawn newspaper reported.
LNG is natural gas that has been cooled to around minus 162 degrees Celsius, turning it into a liquid and reducing its volume by about 600 times. This makes it easier to store and transport by specialised ships.
At its destination, the LNG is converted back into gas through a process called regasification and supplied to consumers. It is used to generate electricity, fuel industrial processes, produce fertilisers and provide energy for heating and cooking. It is also used as a fuel in some vehicles and ships.

articles.title: SC says 'don't travel by air', refuses urgent hearing on airfare hike plea
articles.summary:
Don't travel by air, the Supreme Court told a petitioner on Monday while refusing urgent listing of a plea alleging nearly 700 per cent increase in airfares.
An advocate mentioned the matter for urgent listing before a bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Aparesh Kumar Singh.
"The aviation fare has increased by 700 per cent," the advocate said.
"Don't travel by air," the bench observed.
The advocate then said air travel is an essential service. "It's a violation of Article 14."
Article 14 of the Constitution deals with equality before law.
The apex court is already hearing a separate petition filed by social activist S Laxminarayanan, who has sought a robust and independent regulator that ensures transparency and passenger protection across the civil aviation sector and regulatory guidelines to control "unpredictable fluctuations" in airfare and ancillary charges imposed by private airlines in India.

articles.summary:
In a setback to the Aam Aadmi Party ahead of the Punjab assembly polls, three of its leaders from the state, including Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh and two other legislators, joined the BJP on Monday.
Earlier in the day, suspended AAP MLA and former IPS officer Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh said he resigned as a legislator of the Punjab Vidhan Sabha.
In a post on Facebook, Singh -- the MLA from Amritsar North seat -- said he has sent his resignation to Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan.
Singh, along with Punjab MLAs Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, joined the BJP in the presence of senior leaders at its headquarters here.
His resignation from the Punjab Assembly came on the heels of two other AAP legislators -- Chetan Singh Jouramajra from Samana and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra from Sanour in Patiala district -- resigning from the party on Sunday.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu tracker: Where is the storm now?
articles.summary: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu moved west-northwestwards at a speed of 22 kmph over the west-central and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal during the six hours preceding 8:30 am IST on Monday, November 2, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. At the time, the cyclone was centred near latitude 14.1°N and longitude 81.4°E, approximately 160 km east-southeast of Nellore, 180 km northeast of Chennai, 180 km east-southeast of Kavali, 210 km southeast of Ongole and 240 km south of Machilipatnam.The IMD said Murasu is likely to continue moving northwestwards and cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast as a severe cyclonic storm, with sustained wind speeds of 100–110 kmph and gusts reaching 120 kmph. Landfall is expected between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, from around 11:30 pm on November 2 to the early hours of November 3, 2026.The IMD has warned of heavy rainfall and strong winds along the storm's projected path. Southern Odisha is also expected to receive heavy rainfall, prompting disaster response teams to remain prepared in vulnerable areas.— Indiametdept (@Indiametdept) Also Read: Weather today, November 2: IMD warns of heavy rain in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu; Delhi-NCR's AQI becomes 'severe'; check latest IMD update and AQI levelsCyclone Murasu tracker: Where is the storm now?As of 5:30 am on November 2, Murasu was positioned over the west-central and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal, near 13.9°N latitude and 81.8°E longitude. It had moved west-northwestwards at 25 kmph during the previous six hours and was approximately 200 km from Chennai.The storm's proximity to the Andhra Pradesh coast has brought the landfall forecast into focus. The IMD expects Murasu to continue moving northwestwards before crossing the coast as a severe cyclonic storm. Its projected landfall zone is between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, with the crossing likely to begin around 11:30 pm on November 2 and continue into the early hours of November 3. The forecast wind speed is 100–110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph.Cyclone Murasu tracker: Landfall forecast and expected wind speedThe IMD has forecast that Murasu will maintain its northwestward movement towards the southern Andhra Pradesh coastline. The system is expected to cross the coast as a severe cyclonic storm, bringing strong winds to the landfall region.The projected wind speed of 100–110 kmph, with gusts of up to 120 kmph, could affect areas along the coast during the passage of the storm. The landfall window extends from late Monday night, November 2, to early Tuesday morning, November 3.Cyclone Murasu tracker: Heavy rainfall forecast in Odisha, NDRF and ODRAF on standbyThe IMD has forecast rainfall of 7–20 cm in southern Odisha districts on November 2 and 3 under the influence of the cyclone. Wind speeds in the state are also expected to reach 50–60 kmph, with gusts of up to 70 kmph on November 3.The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) personnel have been kept ready in vulnerable locations to respond to emergencies. Fishermen have been advised against venturing into the sea from November 2 to 4.In Ganjam, officials were directed to ensure that essential supplies were stocked and residents in high-risk areas were moved to safer shelters by Sunday night, November 1.

Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds increased 6.5 per cent year-on-year to Rs 27,934 crore in October.
After adjusting for refunds, net GST collections rose 26 per cent to over Rs 2.03 lakh crore in October.

articles.title: AI bargains with AI: The next great bazaar
articles.summary: In the market, humans meet humans to buy, sell and make deals. The next great bazaar may be where our Al agents haggle for milliseconds Walk through any Indian bazaar and bargaining is de rigueur. The shopkeeper names a price with wounded dignity, the buyer laughs derisively, threatens to walk away, comes back, talks about another shop and, eventually, both parties settle somewhere between offence and satisfaction. The transaction seems purely economic, but it is also social, rich in stories and psychological and emotional, and very human.Now imagine if neither of them is human.Also read: E-commerce firms turn to AI to solve for Bharat during festive salesYour AI agent has already discovered the product, compared alternatives, checked reviews and decided what you are willing to pay. The seller's AI knows inventory, margins, demand and how badly it needs the sale. The two agents bargain for milliseconds, settle on a price and complete the transaction. You receive a message: "Bought it. Saved you 12%."This is no longer science fiction. Personal agents such as Instinct, Meta's Muse and Open AI's Dots are moving AI from answering questions to doing things on our behalf, as you move from asking the AI to tasking the AI.Muse can browse, book and buy with permission. Instinct, which lives inside your WhatsApp, can arrange travel, buy groceries and manage subscriptions.Open AI's Dots are designed as always-on agents with their own cloud computers and access to connected applications. These are early steps towards what an agent really means: software to which we give agency.Also read: AI-aided gifting, self-love light up Zoomer DiwaliEra of negotiationThe next step is obvious. Why merely search and buy when the agent can negotiate? That possibility has moved from speculation to serious research. The Financial Times recently reported that Anthropic is consulting lawyers on how AI agents should negotiate for users, including prices, contracts and disputes.Experiments found that more aggressive agents sometimes got better outcomes, while cooperative ones occasionally gave up individual advantage to reach an agreement. Visa is already talking about "business-to-AI" commerce; more than half the business leaders it surveyed said they were ready for AI-to-AI negotiation.This could change commerce more profoundly than another shopping chatbot.First, the internet itself will have to change. Amazon, Flipkart, or a B2B procurement platform, is designed today to persuade humans. There are glossy pictures, seductive descriptions, stories, influencer videos, recommendations and carefully designed buttons. Machines care much less about romance. An agent wants structured facts: price, dimensions, warranty, delivery time, return policy, reliability, compatibility and perhaps the seller's willingness to negotiate.Two facesWebsites may therefore acquire two faces: one for humans, rich in stories and emotion, and another for machines, factual, structured and instantly comparable. Search engine optimisation gave us SEO. Agentic commerce may give us something like AEO: agent-engine optimisation. The next customer arriving at your website may never see the website.Bargaining itself becomes democratised. There are people who hate negotiating. A skilled agent could give an ordinary consumer some of the power previously available mainly to corporations and wealthy people - a tireless professional negotiator that knows when to push, when to walk away and what alternatives exist.But that creates a new inequality. What happens when my agent is smarter than yours? The wealthy have always hired better lawyers, brokers and advisers. If the richest people also subscribe to the most capable negotiating models, AI might not remove bargaining inequality but actually industrialise it.This is where John Nash and his famous work on game theory enter the bazaar. Game theory studies how rational actors behave when each person's outcome depends partly on what others do. A Nash equilibrium occurs when neither side gains by changing strategy alone.Human negotiators reach such equilibrium imperfectly, clouded by emotion, incomplete information and ego. AI agents could run thousands of strategies almost instantly.Collusion ConundrumBut there is a darker version. What if the buyer's agent and seller's agent learn that subtle cooperation is more profitable for both agents? Perhaps that is the choice ahead. Agents will increasingly represent us because, for many transactions, they will simply be better at it. They will know our budgets, preferences and histories, and eventually negotiate with other agents that know equally much about the other side.Algorithmic pricing has already raised concerns about tacit collusion. A world of autonomous negotiators makes the question sharper: whose interests are they really optimising?And then there is something less economic but perhaps equally important. Humans like shopping. We wander through bazaars, browse bookstores, discover things we did not know we wanted, argue over carpets and feel triumphant when a shopkeeper finally gives us "the special price only for you". Shopping is not merely procurement. It is entertainment, discovery, status, ritual and human contact.If my agent buys my airline ticket, insurance policy and printer cartridge, I will probably be delighted. If it chooses every restaurant, negotiates every holiday and buys every gift, I may have outsourced not just inconvenience but part of life itself.Perhaps that is the choice ahead. Agents will increasingly repre-sent us because, for many transactions, they will simply be better at it. They will know our budgets, preferences and histories, and eventually negotiate with other agents that know equally much about the other side.The bazaar will not disappear. It may split in two. In one, humans will still wander, haggle, flirt with choices and occasionally overpay for the pleasure of the experience. In the other, invisible agents will negotiate billions of transactions at machine speed.For thousands of years, the market was where humans met humans to bargain. The next great bazaar may be where our machines meet instead.

articles.title: US judge dismisses Trump's multibillion-dollar defamation suit against WSJ
articles.summary:
A federal judge has thrown out President Donald Trump's multibillion-dollar lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and media mogul Rupert Murdoch over a story reporting on his ties to wealthy financier Jeffrey Epstein.
US District Judge Darrin Gayles in Miami dismissed the suit with prejudice on Saturday, ruling that the president did not prove the defendants made defamatory statements with actual malice.
The ruling said the lawsuit was "grasping at straws" as it attempted to "manufacture" flaws in the Journal's investigative reporting.
When a case is thrown out "with prejudice," it cannot be refiled again and the dismissal is permanent and incontrovertible.
The lawsuit was over a story the Journal published last year describing a sexually suggestive letter that the paper said bore Trump's name and was included in a 2003 album compiled for Epstein's 50th birthday.

The bureau said in a statement on Saturday that this week's attack was tied to "malicious cyber activity" by an entity known as TraderTraitor, the same actors behind a USD 1.5 billion Bybit hack last year.
The FBI asked crypto exchanges, blockchain analytics companies and others to block transactions linked to various addresses to make sure the money is not laundered to cover up its origins.
It also said its probe found that TraderTraitor was converting stolen assets primarily into a cryptocurrency called ethereum. The FBI expects that TraderTraitor will now attempt to convert the assets using DeFi and "instant swap services."
